name: Ab Crunch
steps: Lie on back with bent knees/elevated feet, hands lightly behind head or across chest, and low back on floor.
Curl shoulder blades a few inches up by bringing ribs toward hips, pause, then lower slowly.

name: Ab Roller
steps: Start on your knees, with your arms straight and the ab roller placed directly under your shoulders and your knees bent at 90 degrees with your hips right above your knees. Before rolling out, tilt your pelvis backwards by thinking about pulling your belly button towards your spine. This should round your back slightly but will better activate your lower abs and protect your lower back.

From here, maintain that position in your hips, squeeze your abs, and slowly roll the wheel out in front of you. Go only as far as you can without letting your lower back cave in. If it does, you’ve gone too far.

To roll back, don’t just move your hips back . Keep your hips locked in place, and pull yourself back with your core. Think about a string lifting your back. Keep going until you reach the starting position, then continue for more reps.
cues: Start with short roll-outs until you build the strength to move further out.

name: Arm Circles
steps: Swing your arms forward in a circular motion for 5 reps and then repeat in the reverse direction.
cues: This exercise is to warm up and mobilize the shoulder joint.
tips: This exercise is to warm up and mobilize the shoulder joint.

name: Arnold Press
steps: Set up an incline bench at about a 60 to 75 degree angle, typically 2 to 3 notches down from the highest position. Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on the bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs. Kick the dumbbells up one at a time to get them up just over your shoulders. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Bring your elbows forward slightly to about a 45 degree angle in front of your body.
Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. Press the weight up until your arms are straight and positioned directly over your shoulders.

As the dumbbells come back down to the starting position, rotate the dumbbells until your palms face you. Then press the weights back up as before, but now rotating the dumbbells so that your palms face away from you at the top position.

name: Asian Squat
steps: Get a rolled up towel and place your heels on it.

Using a squat stance which is typically just outside shoulder width, squat down into however deep is comfortable for you. Keep your chest up and try to keep your heels down. If your heels do come up, you can roll up the towel to make it even thicker, otherwise that’s fine to keep your heels up if you have to.
Place your arms on the inside of your legs and use your elbows to push your knees out. Sit in this position for 30 seconds.

For the next 30 seconds, move side to side to stretch out each ankle one at a time. As you do this, avoid collapsing your knees in and avoid pointing your feet too far outwards as this takes the stretch away from the ankles. Instead, try to keep your feet angled out at a max about 30-45 degrees out and keep each knee inline with the outside of your toes.
cues: Over time try to get to the point where you no longer need a towel under your heels. Also, to deepen the stretch of the hips during the first 30 seconds, you can place your arms in a prayer position. Once that gets easy, place your hands together into fists. Each progression will open up your hips more and more by spreading out the distance between your elbows.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Ups
steps: Take your band, throw it over the bar, and then loop it back through the band to secure it around the bar and tighten it. Then lift one of your legs up and place your foot into the band. Grip the bar using an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and then hang from the bar with both of your legs now fully straightened. From here, place your other foot into the band as well with both feet together. Flex your quads and glutes and contract your abs.

Initiate the pull by first bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears. Pull your elbows down and back into your sides. Think about trying to bring your chest up towards the bar. Continue pulling-up until your chin is above the bar. Control yourself by letting your elbows move up and out until your arms are almost fully straightened, and then continue into your next rep. Take your feet out of the band when you’ve finished your reps.
cues: The thicker the band, the easier this exercise will be. Test out the band to see what provides just the right amount of assistance to enable you to do between 6-12 challenging reps in a row. You can also make it more challenging by taking one foot out from the band to decrease the amount of assistance you get.

name: Band External Rotations
steps: Use either a band attached to a pole or a pulley system with the handle set up at elbow height.
Stand beside the cable pulley or band and externally rotate the shoulder while keeping your elbow at 90 degrees and pinned to the side of your body. Control back to the starting position and repeat.
cues: This exercise is to warm up the rotator cuff muscles.
tips: This exercise is to warm up the rotator cuff muscles.

name: Band Over-And-Backs
steps: Hold your band a little wider than shoulder-width apart.

Bring the band over your head and back behind your body while keeping your arms straight. Keep the tension even as you move the band behind you (don’t “release the slack” by relaxing or resting your hands on your back/butt), and then bring it back over your head into the starting position.
If this is too difficult, widen your hand position. When it gets too easy, narrow your hand position. Avoid arching your back as you perform the movement by slightly contracting your core.
cues: This exercise is to mobilize the chest/shoulder area and help with shoulder/scapular stability.
tips: This exercise is to mobilize the chest/shoulder area and help with shoulder/scapular stability.

name: Band Pull-Aparts
steps: Hold your band at around shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip. Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your upper traps relaxed as you do so and focus on feeling your mid-back muscles working.
Control back to the starting position and repeat. You can use just one strand of the band OR a wider grip to make it easier, then narrow your grip over time.
cues: This exercise is to warm up the mid-back and rotator cuff musculature to help with your pressing.
tips: This exercise is to warm up the mid-back and rotator cuff musculature to help with your pressing.

name: Banded Bent Over Row
steps: Step on the middle of the band and grab it from both sides. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it double banded. Hinge forward at your hips and slightly bend your knees.
Begin your row by pulling with your lats, imagining there is a pencil between your shoulders that you have to squeeze.

Keep your elbows tight to your body and ensure you are not shrugging your shoulders. Slowly return back to the starting position. To make the movement more difficult overtime, you can grab the band closer to provide more resistance.
cues: Progression: Step on the band with one foot and move your other leg back behind you almost in a lunge position. Grab the band with one arm, slightly hinge at your hips and perform a single arm row. Pull with the opposite arm as your front leg.

name: Banded Bent Over Row (Rest-Pause)
steps: Step on the middle of the band and grab it from both sides. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it double banded. Hinge forward at your hips and slightly bend your knees.
Begin your row by pulling with your lats, imagining there is a pencil between your shoulders that you have to squeeze.

Keep your elbows tight to your body and ensure you are not shrugging your shoulders. Slowly return back to the starting position. To make the movement more difficult overtime, you can grab the band closer to provide more resistance.
cues: Progression: Step on the band with one foot and move your other leg back behind you almost in a lunge position. Grab the band with one arm, slightly hinge at your hips and perform a single arm row. Pull with the opposite arm as your front leg.
tips: Progression: Step on the band with one foot and move your other leg back behind you almost in a lunge position. Grab the band with one arm, slightly hinge at your hips and perform a single arm row. Pull with the opposite arm as your front leg.

name: Banded Bicep Curls
steps: Stand on the middle of the resistance band and grab it with both hands so that your hands are in a supinated or underhand grip. Keep your arm straight and your elbow locked, close into the side of your body. If you have a loop/closed band, step on it double banded for more resistance and single banded for less resistance.
Drop your shoulders down away from your ears and curl the band using your bicep maintaining that underhand grip on the band. Don’t allow for your elbow to flare out as you perform the curl.
Return to the starting position allowing the band to create tension on the eccentric movement downwards. Repeat movement.
cues: To progress this exercise, grab the band closer to your feet to create more tension.

name: Banded Bicep Curls (Rest-Pause)
steps: Stand on the middle of the resistance band and grab it with both hands so that your hands are in a supinated or underhand grip. Keep your arm straight and your elbow locked, close into the side of your body. If you have a loop/closed band, step on it double banded for more resistance and single banded for less resistance.
Drop your shoulders down away from your ears and curl the band using your bicep maintaining that underhand grip on the band. Don’t allow for your elbow to flare out as you perform the curl.
Return to the starting position allowing the band to create tension on the eccentric movement downwards. Repeat movement.
cues: To progress this exercise, grab the band closer to your feet to create more tension.
tips: To progress this exercise, grab the band closer to your feet to create more tension.

name: Banded Deadlift
steps: Step on the middle of the band with both feet and slide your feet across it so that your feet are just inside shoulder width. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it double banded. Bend down to grab both sides of the band by pushing your hips back and slightly bending your knees. Engage your core and ensure your back is straight at this bottom position.
While maintaining a neutral back and a slight bend in your knees, drive your feet into the floor, to push your hips forward and extending through the legs in one fluid motion.
Return back to starting position by driving your hips back and creating that slight bend in your knees.
cues: Progression: In order to progress this exercise, simply grab closer down on the band to create more resistance.

name: Banded Donkey Kicks
steps: Place mini-band around knees and set all-fours position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace, lift one bent-knee leg while keeping foot flat as if kicking ceiling until upper thigh is parallel with torso, then return.
cues: Start with lightest band and progress resistance gradually.

name: Banded Face Pulls
steps: Knot band, anchor over top of a closed door, grip each end, and roll shoulders back/down.
Without shrugging, pull band to forehead in a near-90-degree W shape, then slowly return and repeat.
cues: Alternative: stand on mid-band, hinge, and pull toward forehead in a W shape.

name: Banded Goblet Squat
steps: Step on the middle of the band and slide your feet across it so that your feet are about shoulder width apart. Step on a single band and pull the other side of the band up and over your head resting it on your shoulders.

Engage your core, push your glutes back while bending your knees to begin the descent, ensuring your feet are planted on the ground. Squat until you are just at or below parallel to the ground and hold this position for 2-3 seconds.
Maintaining a strong core and a neutral back, drive back up using your quads and glutes and return to starting position.

name: Banded Hamstring Curls
steps: Tie a knot at the end of the band and loop it through the space at the bottom of a door. Wrap the band around your ankles and make sure it is secure. Lay flat on your stomach and slide yourself away from the door to create tension in the resistance band.

From a straight leg position, curl both legs all the way up, so that your heels almost reach your glutes. Ensure that you are pulling with your hamstrings and not excessively arching your back to pull the band.
Slowly resist the band as you straighten your legs back to the starting position.
cues: In order to progress this exercise simply set up the exact same way, rather only wrap the band around a single leg, and perform single leg hamstring curls.

name: Banded Hip Abductions
steps: Using a Built With Science mini band or a mini band of your own, wrap it around your knees and sit at the edge of a bench with your knees together and feet just outside shoulder width apart and toes pointed out slightly. You can lean back and hold the bench behind you for support.

Brace your core and using your upper glute muscles, push your knees out against the band as far as you can while keeping your feet planted. Pause at the end position for a second or two and then bring your knees back together before repeating for another rep.
cues: If a bench isn’t available, you can do these standing up. Stand with your feet together, knees slightly bent and torso bent over about 20 degrees forward. Take a step up laterally to your side using your glutes, and then follow up with another step laterally by the other leg. Continue walking laterally until you perform the desired number of reps for the one side before switching and walking the other way. Wrapping the band around your knees makes it easier, and wrapping it around your ankles will make it harder.

name: Banded Kneeling One Arm Row
steps: Loop the resistance band through the side of the door hinge gap and close the door. Grab the band with one arm and get into a half kneel position.
Roll your shoulders back and down to depress shoulder blades and perform rowing movement by pulling the bands using your lats. Ensure your elbows are tucked tight into your side during each rep.
Slowly return your arms back into the starting position allowing the band to stretch out your lats. Repeat movement.
cues: To progress this movement Grab closer on the band to create more tension. If you have a stable fixture other than a door frame, you may also perform the row standing or seated.

name: Banded Kneeling Rear Delt Row
steps: Loop band through door-hinge gap and close door; hold with one arm in half-kneeling position.
Depress shoulder blade and row with elbow high at shoulder height to bias rear delt, then return slowly.
cues: Progress by gripping closer to band; may also be performed standing/seated with a stable alternative anchor.

name: Banded Kneeling Rear Delt Row (Rest-Pause)
steps: Loop the resistance band through the side of the door hinge gap and close the door. Grab the band with one arm and get into a half kneel position.

Roll your shoulders back and down to depress shoulder blades. Then, perform a rowing movement by pulling the band but as you do so, keep your elbow positioned high at about shoulder height as this will better engage the rear delt.
Slowly return your arms back into the starting position and repeat the movement.
cues: To progress this movement, grab closer towards the band to create more tension. If you have a stable fixture other than a door frame, you may also perform the row standing or seated.
tips: To progress this movement, grab closer towards the band to create more tension. If you have a stable fixture other than a door frame, you may also perform the row standing or seated.

name: Banded Lateral Raises
steps: Step on the middle of the band and grab it from both sides. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it single banded. Slightly hinge forward at your hips.
While maintaining the grip of your resistance band, raise both arms out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbows as you raise them to just below or in line with your shoulders.
Ensuring you are not shrugging your shoulders to your ears at the top of the movement, slowly return your arms back down to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Progression: Put the band under one foot or both, depending on the resistance you need and with one hand, grab the resistance band. Slightly hinge forward at your hips and perform the lateral raise with a single arm.

name: Banded Single Arm Lat Pulldown
steps: Anchor knotted band over closed door, kneel, hold one-handed neutral grip, and start with extended overhead arm.
Pull elbow to side while bending torso toward that side, return to near-full extension, and finish one arm before switching.
cues: Progress by gripping closer up on band.

name: Banded Single Arm Overhead Extensions
steps: Stand on the middle of the band. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it single banded. Grab the band from one end and pull it up and over behind your head keeping your elbow bent behind your head.

Using your triceps, extend your arm up over your head. Keep your elbows locked in position, and as close to your head as possible. Ensure that your core is tight and that you are not arching your lower back as you press up.
Keeping your elbows locked, slowly bend your elbows back into the starting position, feeling a stretch through your triceps, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Progress this exercise by placing the band on the ground and stepping on it as a double band and repeating the same set up. You can step on more of the band to increase the resistance as well. and then bending and extending your arm while keeping your elbow locked in position.

name: Banded Split Squat (Glute Focused)
steps: Step on the resistance band with one foot and grab each side of it. If you have a loop/closed band, ensure you are stepping on it double banded. Bring the opposite leg back, keeping it straight and place it slightly behind your lead foot, this will create your split stance. This can be performed single banded if the resistance is too heavy.
Ensure the foot that is standing on the resistance band is planted and your torso is aligned under your hips. Descend by bending your front leg and lowering your back knee towards the ground.
Push back up to the starting position by using your quads and glutes from the front leg, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: In order to progress this exercise, simply grab closer down on the band to create more resistance.

name: Banded Split Squat (Quad Focused)
steps: Stand on band with lead foot, grip both sides, and set opposite leg straight just behind into a split stance.
Keep lead foot planted/torso aligned, lower rear knee, then push through lead-leg quads and glutes to return.
cues: Progress by gripping lower on the band; use a single band if a double loop is too heavy.

name: Banded Standing Reverse Flyes
steps: Grab the band on each side and raise your arms up directly in front of you, palms facing the ground.
Drop your shoulders down and away from your ears. Pull your arms away from each other, spreading the band apart.
Ensure you are not shrugging your shoulders. Slowly return back to the starting position and repeat movement.
cues: Progression: To progress this movement, simple grab more of the band to increase resistance of it.

name: Banded Standing Reverse Flyes (Rest-Pause)
steps: Grab the band on each side and raise your arms up directly in front of you, palms facing the ground.
Drop your shoulders down and away from your ears. Pull your arms away from each other, spreading the band apart.
Ensure you are not shrugging your shoulders. Slowly return back to the starting position and repeat movement.
cues: Progression: To progress this movement, simple grab more of the band to increase resistance of it.
tips: Progression: To progress this movement, simple grab more of the band to increase resistance of it.

name: Banded Standing Underhand Fly
steps: Stand shoulder-width on a single band and use an underhand grip with palm facing away.
Raise the arm up and across body in a fluid chest-driven motion, return slowly, and complete one side before switching.
cues: Wrap band across shoulders and bring hands together at shoulder height without rotating torso.

name: Banded Straight Arm Pulldown
steps: To set the movement up, you want to tie a simple knot at the end of the band, throw it over the top of a door and close it. If this setup doesn’t work for you though, simply tie the band around any high elevated fixture. Take a few steps back from the door, bend your upper body over slightly by hinging at the hips, and engage your core by contracting your abs.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the band down into your sides. As you do this movement keep your chest up and pull with your lats by driving your elbows backwards.
Slowly control your arms back to the starting position while ensuring your arms stay straight, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Progression: To progress this movement, you can stand further away from the door or perform this exact movement but instead using one arm at a time.

name: Banded Straight Arm Pulldown (Rest-Pause)
steps: To set the movement up, you want to tie a simple knot at the end of the band, throw it over the top of a door and close it. name: Banded Tricep Pushdown
steps: Tie a simple knot at the end of the band, throw it over the top of a door and close it. Grab each end of
the resistance band, pull it down so that your elbows are by your sides, take a few steps back from the door, and bend your upper body over slightly. This is your starting position.

Perform a tricep extension by using your arms to extend your arm downwards while keeping your elbows locked in position. Flare the resistance band out to your sides at the very bottom of the movement to create full contraction of the triceps.
Control the band back to the starting position and then repeat.
cues: Progression: Progress this exercise by transitioning to a single arm tricep pushdown. Again, grabbing higher up on the band to create more resistance

name: Banded Tricep Pushdown (Rest-Pause)
steps: Tie a simple knot at the end of the band, throw it over the top of a door and close it. Grab each end of

name: Barbell Back Box Squat (*knee friendly)
steps: Place a bench, box, or any stable platform you can sit on a few feet back from a squat rack. It should be at the level of your knees or slightly higher. Set a barbell in a rack at about the height of your mid-chest. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Duck under the bar and place it over the back of your shoulders, letting it rest on your upper traps. Lift it out of the rack by extending your legs, and then twist the bar to take it off the safety position. From here, set your feet. Your middle of your feet should be directly underneath the bar, but you can experiment with moving them forwards and see if it feels more comfortable. As for foot width, this will vary for everyone, but experiment with a stance that is just outside shoulder-width with your toes pointed outwards at about a 15 degree angle. At this point you should be about a foot or so in front of the bench or box behind you.

Plant your feet firmly into the ground, pull the bar down into your upper back, and engage your core. Take a deep breath in through your nose. From here, squat down by pushing your hips back while bending your knees. Think about sitting back onto the box or bench. Keep your chest high and continue lowering yourself until your butt makes contact with the box or bench. Lightly touch the box with your butt and then while keeping your weight evenly distributed throughout your big toe, little toe, and your heels, exhale as you reverse the movement by extending your legs, thinking about bringing the bar up towards the ceiling and exhaling as you do so.
cues: For the barbell back box squat, since the exercise is quite technical, it is recommended that you watch the exercise tutorial video.

name: Barbell Back Squat
steps: Set the barbell in a rack around mid-chest height; grip slightly wider than shoulder width; place it over the upper traps; walk out in a controlled three-step sequence and establish stance.
Brace, breathe in, squat by bending hips and knees while keeping the bar over the midfoot, even foot pressure, and knees tracking with toes; descend until thighs reach the app-described depth.
Maintain an almost vertical bar path. Torso angle varies by anatomy if the stated cues and mistake avoidance are followed.
cues: Exercise is technical; app recommends watching the tutorial. If depth is difficult, elevate heels on weight plates to assist ankle mobility.

name: Barbell Back Squat Progression
steps: Start by progressing with goblet squats if new to barbell back squats or form is not yet established.
Hold a light kettlebell or dumbbell tight to the chest, set a just-outside-shoulder-width stance with approximately 15-degree toe turnout, brace, and squat with even foot pressure.
Descend to at least parallel or natural depth with knees tracking toes; reverse by extending legs while controlling each repetition and maintaining a neutral spine.
cues: If full depth is difficult, elevate the heels on weight plates.

name: Barbell Bench Press
steps: Set eyes under bar, grip slightly wider than shoulders, retract/depress shoulder blades, plant feet, unrack over shoulders.
Lower with elbows 45–60 degrees from torso along a slightly forward path to chest, then press under control.
cues: Touch chest under control; do not bounce the bar. Use a spotter whenever possible with heavy loads.

name: Barbell Deadlift
steps: Conventional deadlift uses a fairly narrow stance.
Use bumper plates when possible; otherwise elevate the bar so it begins around shin height.
Set feet hip width with toes slightly out and bar over midfoot; hinge to grip with arms straight and overhand grip just outside knees.
Engage lats as if bending the bar, brace, pull slack out, and push feet away from the floor.
Keep back straight/chest up; keep bar close and vertical over midfoot; finish by driving hips through and squeezing glutes; lower by hinging then bending knees after the bar passes them.
cues: Technical movement: watch tutorial. If back rounding persists, lighten load and consider elevating the start on plates; this can help taller people or specific hip structures.

name: Barbell Deadlift Progression
steps: If you have never done barbell deadlift before, or are struggling quite a bit with your form, then we’ll start with learning how to hinge, which is the foundational movement pattern of a deadlift, and then progress to a dumbbell or kettlebell deadlift.
How To Hinge (0:25)

A hinge movement means bending at the hip. It’s important that you learn how to properly hinge to avoid potential injury. To learn this, stand straight with your hands by your side and feet shoulder-width apart. Brace your core as if someone were about to punch your stomach. Then, push your hips back towards the wall behind you while you hinge forward at the hips. Continue pushing your butt back until your torso lowers to about midway between vertical and parallel to the floor. You can slightly bend your knees as you do so. Pause once you get here, and then reverse the motion by contracting your glutes and pushing your hips forward.

Continue practicing this, trying to keep your back in a neutral position throughout the movement rather than excessively arching it or rounding forward. You can imagine as if you had a straight pole connecting the back of your head to your upper back to your lower back. This should stay in one straight line as you hinge.

If you’re having trouble with this, you can use a wall as a guide. To do this, stand with your back facing the wall about three inches away from it. Start hinging at the hips by sticking your butt out until it makes contact with the wall. Make sure to keep a neutral spine and a nice flat back. Once you can do this several times, try stepping out another inch or two and doing it again. Stick with this pattern until you are completely away from the wall and able to do a full hip hinge.
Once you’ve nailed down your hinge, we can now start progressing it with weight by using a dumbbell or a kettlebell.
Dumbbell/Kettlebell Deadlifts (2:18)

Grab a dumbbell or kettlebell and place it in front of you facing up.To grab the dumbbell, practice the hinge movement by bracing your core and then sticking your butt out behind you to lower your torso towards the ground. Keep your back neutral and continue lowering until you’re able pick up the dumbbell with an underhand grip or a kettlebell using an overhand grip. If however you’re unable to reach that far down without rounding your back, then you can elevate the dumbbell onto a platform to shorten the range of motion.

Once you’ve grabbed the dumbbell, while keeping your core braced, think about pushing the floor away with your feet and pushing your hips forward until you fully straighten. From here, repeat the hinge movement by pushing your hips back to lower the weight. If you can touch the ground with the dumbbell without rounding your back, then go into your next rep by again pushing the floor down with your feet and bringing your hips forward. For those who can’t go all the way down, stop when the dumbbell reaches around the level of knees or shins, and then come back up for another rep. You should feel this primarily in your glutes and a bit in your lower back muscles as well.
Continue practicing this and as you get more comfortable, progress it by using a heavier dumbbell.
cues: Once you’re able to do the dumbbell/kettlebell deadlift while holding at least 40 lbs with good form for at least 10 reps in a row, then that’s a good sign that you’re ready for barbell deadlifts.

name: Barbell Good Mornings
steps: Rack bar around mid-chest, use slightly-wider-than-shoulder grip, place bar on upper traps, unrack, and set hip-width stance.
Brace, hinge hips back with slight knee bend and straight back until hamstring stretch or before low-back rounding.
Drive hips forward and keep chest up; start light before increasing load.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
steps: Use a soft platform around knee/shin height and stabilize it if needed. Load a barbell, preferably with bumper plates; beginners can start with the empty bar. Pad the bar for comfort.

Tuck chin and brace. Squeeze glutes before thrusting; keep head and hips aligned, push through heels and move weight vertically. Brace and hold/squeeze one or two seconds at the top; lower under control.
cues: Avoid back arch/rib flare at the top. Keep ribs down with hard abdominal contraction, squeeze glutes, and posteriorly tilt the pelvis at lockout; lighten load if the lower back dominates.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust (Rest-Pause)
steps: Grab a bench or any soft elevated platform that’s about the height of your knees or shins. If needed, put a pair of heavy weight plates behind it to prevent it from sliding back as you perform the movement. Next, grab a barbell, and load each side with weight, ideally using the bigger bumper plates if your gym has those available. If you’re new to this movement, use just the barbell with no weight at first. You’ll also want to use a thick pad or towel and wrap it around the middle of the barbell for comfort. Lay down with your upper back against the bench and the bar sitting over your hips and your hands holding the bar with an overhand grip just outside your legs. From here, set your feet. You want them positioned such that at the top of the hip thrust your knees are bent at a 90 degree angle and your shins are vertical straight on top of your feet. Try a few reps without weight to find the sweet spot position for you. Once you’ve found the right distance, set your feet at about shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, with your toes pointed out at a slight angle.

Tuck your chin down and brace your core. Before initiating the thrust, squeeze your glutes. Then, while keeping your head and hips in a straight line, continue squeezing your glutes as you push through your heels to drive your hips forward to the top position, moving the weight straight up. At the top position, keep your core braced and pause for a second or two while continuing to squeeze your glutes. Control the weight back down by slowly lowering your butt down towards the ground, stopping at about halfway up from the bottom position and then repeating for another rep.
cues: Avoid arching your back and flaring your ribs out especially at the top position, as this will shift the tension to your lower back muscles. Instead, keep your ribs down by contracting your abs hard, and really focus on squeezing your glutes. Ideally you want to try to posteriorly tilt your pelvis as you get to the top position, by tilting your hips upwards using your glutes. If you still struggle with feeling it more in your back, try lightening the weight and focus more on the contraction of your glutes.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust Progression
steps: Use a glute bridge first: lie on back with bent knees and hip-width feet, brace core to flatten low back, stabilize with elbows, squeeze glutes, and lift hips.
Progress to a single-leg glute bridge: maintain glute squeeze and braced core without hip rotation, extend one leg, lower hips, and drive back up through the planted-leg glute.
Once controlled 3x12–15 repetitions with a three-second top pause are achieved, progress to an unloaded barbell hip thrust.
cues: Move to the next progression only after 3 controlled sets of 12–15 repetitions with clear glute engagement.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
steps: Set bar around mid-thigh (or deadlift it into position); use shoulder-width overhand grip, three-step walkout, and shoulder-width stance with slight toe turnout.
Engage lats and abs, hinge hips back with minimal knee bend, keep bar close over midfoot, and stop before the lower back rounds.
Drive hips forward while braced; use a controlled 2–3 second lowering and roughly one-second ascent.
cues: Think about pulling the floor back with heels to improve hamstring engagement.

name: Barbell Row (Lat Focused)
steps: Grab a bar with a narrow underhand grip about shoulder-width apart and your feet set at about hip width apart. While keeping your arms straight, push your hips back, bend your knees slightly, and lean your torso forward without rounding your lower back.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Pull your elbows back behind your body while keeping them as close as possible to your sides, and pull the bar low towards the level of your belly button.
Control the weight back down to the starting position, and then go into your next rep.
cues: To best engage your back muscles, think about pulling with your elbows rather than with your hands.

name: Barbell Row (mid/upper back focused)
steps: Use overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, hip-width stance, hinge with slight knee bend and neutral low back.
Brace/glute squeeze, row elbows 45–60 degrees back to sternum/lower chest while squeezing shoulder blades, then control down.
cues: Use a thumbless grip and pull with elbows for back engagement.

name: Barbell Shrugs
steps: Stand straight with your arms holding the dumbbells by your sides and palms facing inwards. Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shrug your shoulders up to your ears by engaging your upper traps, then control the weight back down. To best engage your upper traps, thinking about shrugging up and back.
cues: Avoid letting your shoulders round forward as you shrug and avoid sticking your neck out each rep. Wrist straps can also be beneficial so you grip doesn’t give out before your traps do.

name: Behind Body Cable Curls
steps: Set handles at the lowest cable position, face away, step forward slightly, and let arms hang straight behind the body toward the cables.
Brace and depress shoulders; keep elbows fixed while curling hands toward shoulders and slightly inward, then control down to fully straight arms.
cues: For one-arm work, stand in front and slightly opposite the cable so it pulls the working arm straight back.

name: Behind Body Cable Curls (Rest-Pause)
steps: Attach a handle to each cable and move it to the lowest position. Face away from the cable and grab the handle in each arm. Take a couple small steps forward and let your arms hang straight slightly behind your body and towards the direction of the cable.

Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and away from your ears, and then while keeping your elbows locked in position, curl your hands up towards your shoulders. As you do so, you should be curling up but also slightly inward to match the direction of the cable. Once your arms reach roughly the level of your chest, control the weight back down until your arms fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: To perform this exercise one arm at a time, if you were curling your right arm for example, you’d stand in front and slightly to the left of the cable so that you can curl your arm straight up with the cable pulling your arm directly back at a straight angle.

name: Belt Squat
steps: Put on the belt and attach it to the machine or loading pin. Stand on the platform with feet about shoulder width. Stand tall and brace your core.

Squat down by bending knees and hips while keeping your torso upright. Go to a depth you can control, then drive up through your feet to stand. Keep your knees tracking over your toes and avoid bouncing at the bottom.

name: Bench Reverse Hyperextensions
steps: Lay your stomach on a flat bench and the top of your hips positioned at the very end of the bench. Hold underneath the bench for stability and keep your knees bent with legs held together.

Brace your core and then kick your heels back and out so that your legs are parallel with your torso and in an upside down Y shape. Hold the end position for a second or two, squeezing your glutes hard, and then come down to the starting position before repeating for another rep. Focus on using your glutes and bringing your legs from narrow to wide.
cues: Avoid raising your legs too high and hyperextending your back. Instead, keep your core engaged and stop each rep once your legs are parallel with your torso.

name: Bent Over Dumbbell Face Pulls
steps: Set up an incline bench to 45 degrees. Grab dumbbells in each hand and lay your chest on the bench with your head hanging over the end of it and your arms straight with your palms facing down towards your feet.

Brace your core and flex your glutes. From here, pull your elbows and hands back while twisting the thumbs so that they point at the ceiling at the top position. At the top position, your arms should make the shape of a “W” and your forearms should be parallel with your torso. Then, extend your arms outward into a Y position and come back to the W. Return to the starting position.
cues: Although the exercise calls for dumbbells, if you don’t have light enough dumbbells, you can use a 2.5 or 5lb weight plate in each hand instead. In addition, a bench will be best for stability, but if you don’t have one, you can instead push your hips back and bend your torso over towards the ground until you reach a roughly 45 degree angle.

name: Bird Dog
steps: Get onto all fours with your hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, and head facing down at the ground in front of you. Your spine should be in a neutral position, with just a very slight arch.

Brace your core, and then without allowing any movement to occur at the low back, kick one of your legs backwards while simultaneously punching the opposite arm forward until they are both fully straightened. Hold this end position for a second or two, come back down to the starting position on all fours, and then repeat with the other arm and leg. Continue alternating until you finish the desired number of reps for each side. Take it slow and control every single rep.
cues: To better engage the core muscles, think about kicking the heel of your foot straight back and make a fist with your arm while contracting your arm muscles. If you are unable to perform the arm and leg movement together, try the modified version with only your legs and then over time try to introduce the arms. Once this becomes easier, you can hold the end position for longer, even up to 10 seconds.

name: Bodyweight Assisted Single Leg Lunge
steps: Grip onto the edge of a table or any elevated platform and get into a lunge position with your rear foot positioned behind you.

While using the table for assistance, lift your back foot off the ground slightly and squat down into a lunge position by bending your front leg while keeping your back leg elevated in the air. At the bottom position, your front shin should be vertical over your front foot.

Push back up into the starting position by extending your front leg using your quadriceps and glutes. Your front foot should not leave the ground, and your back foot should remain elevated in the air.
cues: Regression: To make the movement easier, you can initially use your back foot for assistance by having it touch the ground at the bottom position of each rep and by using the table more for assistance during the way up.

name: Bodyweight Bicycle Kicks
steps: Lie on your back with your arms and legs straight.
Lift your legs to a 90-degree angle. Lift your chest up so that your shoulder blades are slightly off the ground and hold the back of your head with your elbows wide.

Twist from side to side by extending your left leg straight out while twisting your torso so that your left underarm rotates towards your right knee, then reverse this motion and repeat on the other side. Simply think about trying to touch your opposite shoulder to your opposite knee. Your shoulder blades should be completely off the floor and your lower back should be flat against the ground throughout the movement.

name: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squats (Glute Focused)
steps: Grab a backpack stuffed with books/weight or any weighted object and hold it at your chest. Place your back foot on the top of a bench or any elevated platform. Your front foot can then be positioned based on what you want to target. Take a shorter step forward if you want to target the quads more, or a longer step forward if you want to target the glutes more.
After you get your set up right, lower your back knee towards the ground until your front thigh is at least parallel with the ground

Push back up through your front foot. Your heel shouldn’t raise off the floor and you want to keep your head, back, and hips aligned throughout each rep. Your upper body can lean forward slightly. Repeat for more reps.
cues: To progress the movement, you can slow down the downward part of the movement and/or elevated your front foot onto an elevated platform such as a stack of books to increase the range of motion of each rep.

name: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squats (Quad Focused)
steps: Hold a weighted backpack/object at chest and elevate rear foot; choose front-foot position for desired emphasis.
Lower rear knee until front thigh is at least parallel, then push through front foot without heel lift while keeping head/back/hips aligned.
cues: Progress with slower eccentrics and/or front-foot elevation; shorter step biases quads, longer step glutes.

name: Bodyweight Close-Grip Push-Ups
steps: Get down on your knees and set your hands by placing them in a diamond shape close together. Extend your legs one at a time straight behind you with your toes together.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears, engage your core, and flex your thighs and glutes. Maintain this position as you slowly lower your body down while tucking your elbows close to your sides. Continue until your chest almost touches the ground.
From here, push up and back until your arms fully straighten. Let your shoulder-blades open up at the top before proceeding to the next rep.
cues: Avoid excessively arching your back and letting your hips drop. Instead, maintain a straight line from your head to hips to toes by keeping your core, glutes, and quads fully engaged.

name: Bodyweight Close-Grip Push-Ups (Rest-Pause)
steps: Get down on your knees and set your hands by placing them in a diamond shape close together. Extend your legs one at a time straight behind you with your toes together.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears, engage your core, and flex your thighs and glutes. Maintain this position as you slowly lower your body down while tucking your elbows close to your sides. Continue until your chest almost touches the ground.
From here, push up and back until your arms fully straighten. Let your shoulder-blades open up at the top before proceeding to the next rep.

name: Bodyweight Goblet Squats
equipment: backpack stuffed with books or another weighted object
steps: Hold the weighted object at chest height; use a narrow stance with toes forward and optionally elevate the heels for more quad emphasis.
Brace the core and squat down by bending knees and pushing hips back until thighs are at least parallel, taking about 3–5 seconds to descend.
Push back up through quads and glutes to stand; optionally pause at the bottom and slow the movement further.

name: Bodyweight Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lay flat on your back with your feet and arms extended. Move into posterior pelvic tilt by contracting your abs until your lower back is flat against the ground.

Raise your upper body up off the ground by contracting your abs – raise your upper body such that your shoulder blades are not touching the ground. Simultaneously raise your legs up slightly as well in order to make a “C” shape. Your arms should be extended straight out behind you, but ensure that your lower back remains flat. Hold this position while contracting your abs and hold it until your form deteriorates.
cues: Optional (Harder): Raise your upper body up off the ground by contracting your abs – raise your upper body such that your shoulder blades are not touching the ground. Simultaneously raise your legs up slightly as well in order to make a “C” shape. Your arms should be extended straight out behind you, but ensure that your lower back remains flat. Hold this position while contracting your abs and hold it until your form deteriorates.

name: Bodyweight Leg Extension Isometric
steps: Lean your back and butt against a wall.
Lift your heels so that only your toes are touching the floor.
Slide down the wall while allowing your knees to push forward.
Hold this position for 30 seconds.
cues: Ensure that any pain experienced does not exceed a level of three or four out of 10.

name: Bodyweight Lying Leg Raises
steps: Lay flat on your back with your feet together, legs straight, and arms out to your side. Move into posterior pelvic tilt by contracting your abs and squeezing your glutes until your lower black is flattened on the ground.
Raise your legs up by contracting your abs and curling your pelvis towards your belly button until your legs reach around 90-degrees. They should be kept relatively straight as you do so.

Slowly lower your legs down until your feet almost touch the ground. Just before they touch the ground though, raise your legs back up immediately into another rep in order to keep constant tension in the abs. Your lower back should remain flat and not arched throughout the process.
cues: You can progress this movement over time by slowing down the downward portion of each rep as much as possible, and keeping your abs engaged as you do so.

name: Bodyweight Mountain Climbers
steps: Get into a plank position with your arms positioned straight under your shoulders and your legs extended with feet together. Your back should be straight as opposed to excessively arched or rounded.

Using your abs, crunch one of your knees up towards your chest. As you do so, you should flex your spine slightly to engage your abs and to generate the power needed to kick your knee up to your chest.

Switch to the other leg for the next rep, and then repeat going back and forth. Focus on engaging and using your core during each rep as opposed to just using your hip flexors to kick your knees up. And as you perform your reps, especially as you fatigue, ensure that your hips are not raising up and that you’re maintaining a neutral spine throughout.
cues: To progress the exercise, you can perform your reps faster and/or try to kick your knees up higher up on your chest.

name: Bodyweight Pushdown Isometric
steps: Press palms firmly into a sturdy countertop with a slight knee bend.
Hold 30 seconds and monitor pain so intensity does not exceed 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce downward pressure if pain surpasses 4/10.

name: Bodyweight Single Leg Calf Raises
steps: Place the front half of your foot on an elevated platform such as stairs or stacked books. Place one hand on a fixture or structure for support, such as a table or wall.
Drop your heel down to the floor, creating a stretch through your calf muscle. Pause here briefly.

Push up through your calf all the way onto the ball of your foot as if you were standing on your toes and squeeze at the top for a few seconds. Drop back down to the bottom until your heel touches the floor, pause again, and then repeat for more reps. Finish your reps on one side before transitioning to the other leg.

name: Bodyweight Sissy Squat
steps: Grab onto the side of a rack or any fixture for support with one hand and place your feet about shoulder-width apart with your toes facing forward.

Brace your core and then lean your torso back, come up on your toes, and drive your knees as far forward as you can to lower your body. Lower until your torso reaches about a 45-degree angle or as low as you comfortably can. Keep your back straight with your head, hips, and knees in a straight line as you do so. From here, extend your legs back up to the starting position, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: If needed in the beginning, you can use your hand support to assist you on the way up, but the goal is to use as little support as possible with your hand on the way up. Then once you gain the strength, you can consider loading the movement by holding a light dumbbell or weight plate at your chest.

name: Bodyweight Sliding Hamstring Curls
steps: Lay on your back on a smooth surface with your arms by your sides and legs fully extended in front of you. Wear socks and/or place your feet on two cloths or something that will enable them to slide easily.
Using your hamstrings, curl your heels in towards you while raising your hips up into the air. Your back should remain straight as you do so.

Straighten your legs by reversing the movement in a controlled fashion, again keeping your back straight as you do so. Straighten your legs just before they fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep to maintain constant tension on the hamstrings.
cues: Progression: Slow down the tempo and/or perform them with one leg at a time.

name: Bodyweight Sliding Reverse Lunges
equipment: socks and/or paper plate or cloth
steps: On a smooth surface, place the rear foot on a sock, paper plate, or cloth and take a lunge stance; optionally hold a book-filled backpack or other weight at the chest.
Slide the rear foot back while bending the front leg until the front thigh is parallel with the floor.
Slide the rear foot forward while extending the front leg until nearly straight; before it fully extends, immediately begin the next slide-back repetition, keeping the core engaged and back neutral.

name: Bodyweight Step-Ups
steps: Stand in front of a stable bench or box, or anything that you can step on to. It should be ideally between the level of your knees or mid-thighs.

Brace your core and place one foot on the bench. Push down into that foot and stand up until your leg is straight, keeping your other leg just slightly above the platform. Lower yourself down in a controlled manner, bring both feet back together, and then perform another step up with the opposite leg. Continue switching back and forth between legs until you complete the desired number of reps per side.
cues: Avoid using your planted leg to kick yourself up on the way up. Think of that leg as acting simply as a kickstand for balance. You want 80% to 90% of your weight to be on the working leg, and only 10-20% on the back leg.

name: Bodyweight Step-Ups (Glute Focused)
steps: Stand in front of a stable bench or box, or anything that you can step on to. It should be ideally between the level of your knees or mid-thighs.

Brace your core and place one foot on the bench. Push down into that foot and stand up until your leg is straight, keeping your other leg just slightly above the platform. Lower yourself down in a controlled manner, bring both feet back together, and then perform another step up with the opposite leg. Continue switching back and forth between legs until you complete the desired number of reps per side.

name: Bodyweight Tricep Extensions
steps: Start in a push-up position, then drop to forearms roughly beneath shoulder/head level.
Press hands into floor with triceps until arms straighten to full push-up while keeping core engaged/body straight; return to forearms and repeat.
cues: Make it easier from knees and/or start with forearms farther in front of head; progress them toward shoulders.

name: Bodyweight V-Ups
steps: Lay on your back with your hands and legs straight out. Move into posterior pelvic tilt by contracting your abs and squeezing your glutes such that your lower back is flattened against the ground.

Exhale while simultaneously lift your arms and legs straight up until they just about touch in the middle. Don’t worry if you can’t reach them together very far, just go as far as you can by contracting your abs. Try to at least get your shoulder-blades off of the ground as you reach.

Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position by reaching your hands back and controlling your legs down. Ensure that your lower back is still flat against the ground, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: You can progress the movement overtime by slowing down the downward phase, reaching higher up, and adding weight to the movement by holding onto a dumbbell or any weighted object as you reach up.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Glute Focused)
steps: Choose an elevation appropriate to available equipment; tutorial explains options.

Set stance by sitting on bench and extending legs; move the front foot forward 1–2 inches for more glute emphasis. Feet should be hip-width apart rather than in a straight line; use dumbbells if needed and start with weaker leg.
Hold dumbbells by sides, brace with neutral lumbar spine and slight torso lean, descend until front thigh is at least parallel and rear knee almost touches floor, then drive through front heel.
cues: Treat back leg as a kickstand: retain about 80–90% of load in the front leg and 10–20% in the rear leg.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Quad Focused)
steps: Choose elevation, set front/rear feet approximately hip width, and use a stance found by extending legs from a seated bench position; shift back 1–2 inches for quad emphasis.
Hold dumbbells at sides, brace and lean torso slightly forward with neutral back; descend until front thigh is at least parallel and rear knee nearly touches floor, then drive through front heel.
cues: Back leg is only a balance kickstand; retain 80–90% of load on front leg.

name: Cable Crunches
steps: Use a rope attachment and set it to the highest notch at a cable machine. Grab the rope with a neutral grip and kneel 1-2 steps in front of the pulley with your knees bent at a 90 degree angle. Bring your elbows down by your sides and hold the rope behind your head with your hands tucked on either side of your head.

Engage your abs, and then while keeping your hips locked in place, use your abs to curl your chest down towards your knees. Your back should round as you do this and your hips should remain locked in place with your knees still at a 90 degree angle. Control the weight back to the starting position and then repeat for more reps.

name: Cable Curl Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use.
Hold the curl in the middle position for a duration of 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels; it should remain at or below a three or four out of 10.
cues: Reduce the weight if the pain level exceeds a four out of 10.

name: Cable Kickbacks
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a cable machine and move the pulley down to about the level of your knee. Stand facing square a few steps away from the cable machine with the non working leg in line with the anchor point of the cable, and then turn both feet 30 degrees in the direction of the working leg. Hold onto the pole with the arm that’s on the same side as the non-working leg and bend your torso over forward just slightly.

Brace your core and press down on your non working leg for stability. Lift your foot and cross your working leg across the other leg towards the cable. While keeping your leg straight, use your glutes to kick your heel back and out behind you as far as is comfortable. As you do so, you can rotate your foot such that the outside part of your foot faces the ceiling at the end position. Control your leg back to the starting position, again crossing over your non-working leg, and then repeat for another rep. Finish your reps on one side before switching to the other side.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
steps: Attach a handle to the cable and move it to the bottom attachment. Face away from the cable and reach behind your body to grab the handle with one hand. Take a couple steps forward and then a small step sideways towards the direction of your working arm. You should end up with your hand by your thigh with the direction of the cable headed back behind your body.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Keep your arms just slightly bent and raise your arm diagonally at about 15 to 30 degrees in front of your body. Raise until your arm reaches shoulder-height, control back down, and then repeat for more reps. Switch arms after you’ve rested for 30 seconds.
cues: To perform two arms at a time, grab the left cable with your right hand and right cable with your left hand. Turn so you face away from the cable and take a few steps forward. While keeping your arms just slightly bent, raise your arms into a wide Y position in front of you. Raise until your arms reach shoulder-height, control them back down, and then repeat for more reps.

name: Cable Lateral Raise (Rest-Pause)
steps: Attach a handle to the cable and move it to the bottom attachment. Face away from the cable and reach behind your body to grab the handle with one hand. Take a couple steps forward and then a small step sideways towards the direction of your working arm. You should end up with your hand by your thigh with the direction of the cable headed back behind your body.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Keep your arms just slightly bent and raise your arm diagonally at about 15 to 30 degrees in front of your body. Raise until your arm reaches shoulder-height, control back down, and then repeat for more reps. Switch arms after you’ve rested for 30 seconds.

While keeping your arms just slightly bent, raise your arms into a wide Y position in front of you. Raise until your arms reach shoulder-height, control them back down, and then repeat for more reps.

While keeping your arms just slightly bent, raise your arms into a wide Y position in front of you. Raise until your arms reach shoulder-height, control them back down, and then repeat for more reps.

name: Cable Pushdowns (*elbow friendly)
steps: Set a pulley to the highest height. Use two rope attachments and pull them through so that the rope extends longer. Grab one rope in each hand and take two to three steps back from the pulley. From here, with a slight bend at your knees, bend your torso forward about 30 degrees. Bring your elbows down to your sides angled out just slightly and lock them there. Your hands should be around the level of your chest.

Brace your core, and then while keeping your elbows locked in place, use your triceps to extend your arms. You should feel as if you’re pulling the ropes down and out apart. Keep your elbows locked as you control your hands back up to about the height of your chest, and then go down for another rep.
cues: Avoid swaying your elbows back and forth excessively as you perform each rep. Instead, keep your elbows locked in place and only move your forearms. Avoid failing to fully extend your arms on the way back. If needed, lighten the weight so you’re able to fully extend your arms to fully contract your triceps. Avoid keeping your elbows tucked too close to your body and pressing your arms straight down. Instead, angle them out to fully contract your triceps.

name: Cable Pushdowns (*elbow friendly) (Rest-Pause)
steps: Set a pulley to the highest height. Use two rope attachments and pull them through so that the rope extends longer. Grab one rope in each hand and take two to three steps back from the pulley. From here, with a slight bend at your knees, bend your torso forward about 30 degrees. Bring your elbows down to your sides angled out just slightly and lock them there. Your hands should be around the level of your chest.

Brace your core, and then while keeping your elbows locked in place, use your triceps to extend your arms. You should feel as if you’re pulling the ropes down and out apart. Keep your elbows locked as you control your hands back up to about the height of your chest, and then go down for another rep.

Avoid keeping your elbows tucked too close to your body and pressing your arms straight down. Instead, angle them out to fully contract your triceps.

Avoid keeping your elbows tucked too close to your body and pressing your arms straight down. Instead, angle them out to fully contract your triceps.

name: Cable Shrugs
steps: Based on their anatomy, the upper traps move your arms upward and inward. Cables are great because you can use a wide setup to accomplish this upward and inward movement.
Set the cables to their bottom position. Grab each handle and stand in the middle of the cables with the cables pulling your arms directly out to your sides.
Keep your chest up, brace your core, and then while keeping your arms in this angled out position, shrugging your shoulders up and in as far as you can, then control the weight back down.
cues: Avoid letting your shoulders round forward as you shrug and avoid sticking your neck out each rep.

name: Cat Cow
steps: Get onto all fours with your knees under your hips and hands under your shoulders. From here, in a gentle motion, round your back up towards the ceiling as if someone was pulling your mid-back up with a rope. As you do this, take a deep breath in while tucking your head down. Pause at the top position for 1 second.

Then, exhale as you reverse this motion by now curving your back the opposite way while lifting your head up. Pause at the bottom position for 1 second. Each cycle (going from up to down) should take you about 8 seconds to do. Try to get around 7-8 cycles within your 1 minute time frame.
cues: If you’re having trouble nailing down this motion though, try placing a band around your mid-back. This will help pull your spine into the bottom position and then give you the resistance and sensory feedback you may need to learn how to properly round your spine upwards.

name: Chest Dips
steps: Set a dip machine with parallel handles; grip the handles, get to the top position with arms locked and legs bent, engage the core, and lean slightly forward.
Lower slowly by bending elbows behind you; at the bottom squeeze shoulder blades together and go until arms are parallel to the floor or as low as comfortable.
Keep elbows stacked above wrists at the bottom, push through palms, extend elbows, and squeeze the chest to return to the start.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
steps: Set up an incline bench to an angle of about 30 degrees, typically the second notch up from the bottom. Grab a pair of dumbbells and lay your chest on the bench so that your head extends off the end of the bench with your arms hanging down by your sides. Plant the balls of your feet firmly into the ground with your legs fully straightened or slightly bent.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears, squeeze your glutes, and flex your abs. From here, pull your elbows back behind your body at about a 45 degree angle away from your torso. Continue pulling as far back as you can. Pause briefly at the end position, control the weight back down to the starting position with your arms straight, and then go into your next rep.

name: Chest Supported Machine Row
steps: Set seat so wide-overhand grip pulls elbows 45–60 degrees; select wider grip if available.
Depress shoulders, row elbows back 45–60 degrees while squeezing shoulder blades, then control forward.
cues: Use a thumbless grip and pull with elbows to increase back activation; use wide overhand grip or choose an alternative if only narrow neutral grip exists.

name: Chest Supported Machine Row (Rest-Pause)
steps: If the machine has a seat, adjust the seat to a height such that when using a wide overhand grip, when your elbows pull back, they will make an angle of about 45 to 60 degrees. Once you’ve figured out the proper seat height, if the machine has a wider overhand grip, use that grip position. If the machine only has a narrow neutral grip available, then choose an exercise alternative otherwise it won’t hit the target muscles very well.

name: Chin-Ups
steps: Grip the bar using an under hand grip roughly shoulder-width apart. From here, let your body hang and then begin stabilizing your body by bringing your feet together, flexing your quads and glutes and contracting your abs. You want to maintain this position as you pull.

Initiate the pull by first bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears. Then, pull your elbows down and back into your sides as if you were trying to pull them into your back pockets. As you do this, think about trying to bring your chest up towards the bar. Continue pulling-up until your chin is above the bar. From here, control yourself down until your arms are almost fully straightened, and then continue into your next rep.
cues: Once you can do 10 chin-ups in a row, you can start to add weight to the movement by using either a weight belt or by holding a light dumbbell between your feet.

name: Close Grip Dumbbell Press
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells, lay on a flat bench, and bring your arms straight over your shoulders with your palms facing each other. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and then back together to create a little bit of space between your lower back and the bench.

Control the weight down towards your lower chest by tucking your elbows close to your sides. Continue lowering until the weights reach around the level of your torso, or as low as is comfortable for you. Use your triceps to extend your arms straight up until they are fully locked out and directly over your shoulders.
cues: Avoid holding the weights together at the top position. Instead keep constant tension on the triceps by immediately proceeding to your next rep as soon as your arms fully straighten. Avoid letting gravity drop the weight on the way down. Instead, control the weight down by using your triceps.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
steps: Use normal bench setup but a shoulder-width, narrower-than-normal grip; retract/depress shoulders and plant feet.
Lower to lower chest with elbows close, then press up/back to lockout while keeping chest up, scapulae set, and glutes on bench.
cues: Keep wrists stacked, elbows tucked, and touch chest under control—do not bounce.

name: Close-Grip Smith Machine Press
steps: Place a flat bench underneath the bar. Rack the bar into its starting position so that when you grab the bar, your elbows are just slightly bent. Grip the bar with an overhand narrow grip, about shoulder-width apart, and narrower than your normal bench press grip. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and then back together. Firmly plant your feet on the ground. Unrack the bar by lifting it up slightly and twisting the bar to get it into the unlocked position.

While tucking your elbows close to your sides, control the weight down towards your lower chest until it makes contact with your body. After you reach the bottom position, push the bar up and back to the starting position with your arms fully locked out.
cues: Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides. Instead, keep your elbows tucked closed to your sides to best engage the triceps. Avoid bouncing the bar against your chest at the bottom position. This is the most important part of the movement for growth, so use control and simply touch your chest.

name: Close-Grip Underhand Lat Pulldown
steps: Set thigh pad, use shoulder-width underhand grip, sit tall with chest up and torso still.
Depress shoulders then pull bar to upper chest by driving elbows down/back; return until arms are straight with lat stretch.
cues: Avoid leaning far back or swinging.

name: Cross Cable Tricep Extensions
steps: Set two pulleys to the highest notch with no attachment. You’ll be grabbing onto the ball at the end of the pulley as your handle. While facing towards the cable machine, grab the left side with your right hand, grab the right side with your left hand, and then take a few steps back. Slightly bend at your knees and bend your torso forward about 30 degrees. Bring your elbows down to your sides and lock them there. Your hands should be around the level of your chest with the cables crossed over in front of you.

Brace your core, lock your elbows in place, and use your triceps to extend your arms. At the end position, your arms should be fully straight and angled slightly away from your sides. Keep your elbows locked as you control your hands back up to about the height of your chest, and then go down for another rep.
cues: Avoid swaying your elbows back and forth excessively as you perform each rep. Instead, keep your elbows locked in place and only move your forearms.

name: Curtsy Lunges
equipment: slightly elevated platform or weight plate (optional)
steps: Stand on a slightly elevated platform such as a weight plate with feet about hip width and toes forward.
Brace the core, take one leg slightly out and back into a lunge, keeping the rear foot up and roughly a foot or two outside the planted leg.
Push through the planted leg to return with feet together; complete repetitions on one side, then switch legs.

name: Dead Bug
steps: Keep core engaged, extend opposite arm and leg, hold the position a moment, go back to the starting position and repeat changing sides.
cues: This exercise is used to mobilize and warm up the core, shoulders, and legs.

name: Dead Hang
steps: Hang from a pull up bar with your arms straight. Keep your body as still as possible and don’t swing. Use a grip you can hold safely and breathe steadily.
Completely relax your back and shoulders to get a full stretch.

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
steps: Sit with dumbbells, kick them to arms-straight position, retract and depress shoulder blades, create a small lower-back arch, and brace.
Lower with elbows about 60 degrees from torso until weights reach torso level or a comfortable depth.
Press with the chest until arms lock out over shoulders, thinking of drawing the arms together.
cues: Slightly decline a movable flat bench with a 25 lb plate below its front, keep chest up, and avoid flaring elbows.

name: Decline Machine Chest Press
steps: Bring your elbows up to about a 60 to 70 degree angle from your body. Wherever your hands end up is the level you want the handles to be, so adjust your seat until you get that right. Use a fairly wider grip outside of shoulder-width. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and pinch them together.

Push the handles slightly into the starting position such that your elbows are by your sides and are tucked at roughly a 60 to 70 degree angle from your torso. Brace your core and push the handles until your arms fully lockout. Control the weight back down to the starting position and repeat.

name: Decline Push-Ups (bands optional)
steps: Cross/loop band backpack-style so it forms an X across back and hook each band with thumbs; elevate feet on a platform and use slightly-wider-than-shoulder-width grip.
Depress shoulders, brace/core and flex thighs/glutes, lower with elbows 45–60 degrees until chest nearly touches ground, then press to straight arms and let shoulder blades open at top.
cues: Progress using a thicker band or up to 30 repetitions per set.

name: Decline Weighted Sit Ups
steps: Sit on a decline bench with your lower legs secured under the pads and your hands across your chest. Ensure that you aren’t arching your back when in this starting position.
Slowly lower your upper body back until your hips are almost fully extended.

Raise your body by contracting your abs until your torso is upright. Again, ensure you are not arching your back as you lift your torso up – this is an indication that your abs may not be strong enough for the movement. To make it easier, you can lessen the decline of the bench.

name: Deep Squat
steps: Hold a weight plate in front of your chest in a deep squat, rocking side to side over each ankle in a soft and constant motion for 30 seconds.
cues: This exercise is used to mobilize and warm up the hips and leg muscles for your leg movements, focusing on your hips and ankles.

name: (Bodyweight) Dip Push-Ups
steps: Get into a push-up position on the floor and elevate your hands on a stack of books or any elevated platform.

While keeping your elbows slightly tucked rather than flared out to your sides, push your arms downward to raise your upper body into an upward position until your arms straighten, while just letting your lower body slide along for the ride.
Return back to the starting position by bending your arms and letting your lower body slide back.
cues: These can be progressed by either elevating the platform used (e.g. use chairs) and/or wearing a weighted bag or looping a band around your neck and hands to provide more resistance as you push up.

name: Dumbbell Chest Supported Row (mid/upper back focused)
steps: Set up an incline bench to an angle of about 30 degrees, typically the second notch up from the bottom. Grab a pair of dumbbells using a thumbless grip and lay your chest on the bench with your arms hanging down by your sides and palms facing each other. Plant the balls of your feet firmly into the ground with your legs fully straightened or slightly bent.

To stabilize your body, bring your shoulders down and away from your ears, squeeze your glutes and flex your abs. Then, pull your elbows back behind your body at about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your torso. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top position.
Control the weight back down to the starting position instead of letting it just drop. Let your shoulder blades open up, reset, and then go into your next rep.
cues: Think about pulling with your elbows each rep in order to better activate your back.

name: Dumbbell Curl Isometric
steps: Select a lighter-than-normal dumbbell and hold the curl at its midpoint for 30 seconds.
Monitor pain; it should not exceed 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce load if pain exceeds 4/10.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
steps: Lay back on the ground with knees bent and squeeze your shoulder blades together.

Bring dumbbells over your shoulders so they're stacked. Lower the dumbbells with control so that you make a 30-45 degree angle with your arms. Lower the dumbbells until your triceps just touch the floor.
Drive the dumbbells up and squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Fly
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and lay on a flat bench with your arms straight above you and palms facing each other. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and pinch them together to create a small space between your lower back and the bench.

Slowly lower the weight directly out to your sides while bending at your elbow. Continue lowering until your elbows reach the level of your torso. From here, use your chest to bring your arms together back to the starting position. Stop when your arms are directly over your shoulders and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Lay back on bench, pinch shoulder blades together, lower weights with bent elbows and bring back to center

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raises
steps: Use shoulder-width stance, slight knee bend, and roughly 15-degree torso lean.
Raise slightly bent arms in a Y 15–30 degrees in front to shoulder height, then lower under control.
cues: A thumbless grip and thinking of pushing hands outward can improve activation.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raises (Rest-Pause)
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and knees slightly bent. Lean your torso forward about 15 degrees.

Brace your core. While keeping your arms just slightly bent, raise your hands out in front of you. As you do so, raise your arms in a Y position in front of you. This is about 15 to 30 degrees in front of your body. Raise the weight until your arms reach shoulder-height, control them back down until your hands are down in front of your thighs, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: To better help with muscle activation, you can try using a thumbless grip and rather than thinking about raising the weight up, think about raising the weight out as if you were pushing your hands out towards the walls.
