name: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curls
steps: Secure a light dumbbell between feet while prone on a flat bench, holding a bench leg for stability.
Brace and pull down on the bench; curl with hamstrings to just short of 90 degrees, then lower until legs are nearly extended. The short range maintains hamstring tension.
cues: Do not curl past 90 degrees: hamstrings are no longer involved past that point and a dropped dumbbell is risky.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extensions
steps: Using one weight only, grab the dumbbell with both hands cupping the dumbbell head and start with elbows bent and dumbbell behind your head. Both elbows should be bent at about a 90 degree angle.

Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and maintain a neutral spine. Lift the dumbbell up above your head by contracting your triceps and fully extending at the elbow. At this top position, your arms should be fully extended and parallel with the body.
Lower the weight back behind your head to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
steps: Set bench 2–3 notches from bottom for a 45–60 degree angle and position most of the upper arm on the bench with a dumbbell in one hand.
Lower slowly while retaining biceps tension; dumbbell should hover slightly above bench at bottom.
Contract biceps to curl back to start while maintaining a fixed wrist.

name: Dumbbell Pullovers
steps: Lay your upper back on the edge of a bench, and keep your upper body parallel to the ground by bending your knees to 90 degrees and engaging your core. Hold the dumbbell straight overhead such that your arms are straight and the dumbbell is positioned vertically.
Keeping your body upright and core engaged, slowly lower your arms overhead until your biceps roughly reach the level of your ears. Keep your arms straight or slightly bent as you do so.

By thinking about driving/pulling your elbows forward, slowly bring your arms back to above your chest as in the starting position by contracting your lats. You will feel this in your chest as well, but you should feel your lats engaging as you pull the weight back up to the starting position.
cues: If you don’t have access to a bench, these can be performed on the floor instead by holding the dumbbell sideways to ensure you still are getting a sufficient range of motion (see tutorial video for more info).

name: Dumbbell Reverse Flyes
steps: While seated at the edge of a bench or chair, bend your upper body forwards such that your torso is at roughly a 45-degree angle with the ground. Grab a pair of dumbbells in each hand and position them in between your legs with you arms straight. Your back should ideally be neutral, but a slight rounding in the back is fine.

While keep your arms just slightly bent, raise the dumbbells out to your sides while rotating your hands such that your pinkies point towards the ceiling at the top position. IF this is uncomfortable on your shoulder, you can simply raise without the rotation such that your palms remain facing the floor at the top position.
Return back to the start position in a controlled fashion, then repeat for more reps.
cues: Alternative: If you don’t have access to a bench, these can instead be performed standing and bent-over rather than seated on a bench.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells, hold them by your sides, and take a shoulder-width stance with your feet pointed slightly outwards at about a 15 degree angle.

Contract your abs, take a deep breath in through your nose, then descend by pushing your hips straight back. Keep just a very slight bend at your knees and keep the bar as close to your body as possible, ideally right above the middle of your feet. As you descend, your hands should move from a neutral position at your sides to your palms facing towards you with the dumbbells held horizontally in front of your legs. Lower the dumbbells only until the point where you can’t push your hips back without your lower back starting to round, usually at knee level or mid-shin level.

Keep your core braced and then exhale as you reverse the motion by pushing your hips forward and then rotating the dumbbells back into the starting position by your sides. Once your legs are fully straight, repeat for another rep. Spend about 2-3 seconds on slowly controlling the weight down, and then about 1 second to bring the weight back up.
cues: To better engage the hamstrings, you can think about pulling the floor back with your heels as you come up.

name: Dumbbell Shrugs
steps: Stand straight with your arms holding the dumbbells by your sides and palms facing inwards. Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shrug your shoulders up to your ears by engaging your upper traps, then control the weight back down. To best engage your upper traps, thinking about shrugging up and back.
cues: Avoid letting your shoulders round forward as you shrug and avoid sticking your neck out each rep. Wrist straps can also be beneficial so you grip doesn’t give out before your traps do.

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Rear Delt Row
steps: Position yourself in front of a flat bench or any elevated platform with a dumbbell placed in front of it. Get into a squat stance and then lean into the bench by tipping yourself over and grabbing the bench with one arm to stabilize your body. With your other arm, grab the dumbbell and get into the starting position with your back neutral and head facing down.

Brace your core, and then pull your elbow back towards your shoulder, keeping your elbow flared out. From here, lower the weight back down to the starting position and repeat. Finish your reps on one side before switching to the other side.

name: Dumbbell Spider Curls
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on an incline bench with the backrest set at a 45-60 degree angle. Let your arms hang down by your sides and plant your feet firmly on the ground under your knees.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. While keeping your elbow locked into place, with one arm curl the weight up towards your shoulders. As you do so, rotate your palms so that they face up towards the ceiling at the top position. Lower the weight back down to the starting position, letting your wrists rotate back into a neutral position, and then repeat with the other arm. Start each set with your weaker arm and continue alternating arms every rep until you complete the required number of reps for each arm.
cues: Avoid swinging your body and elbows forward and back and excessively as you curl. Instead, lighten the weight, keep your elbow locked in place and control the weight. A little bit of forward elbow movement is fine, but it shouldn’t be excessive. Avoid letting gravity drop the weight for you on the way down. Instead, use your biceps to slowly control the weight back down to the starting position before starting your next rep.

name: EZ-Bar Bicep Curl
steps: Stand tall holding the EZ bar with a comfortable grip. Keep your elbows close to your sides and your shoulders relaxed. Brace your core and keep your torso still.
Curl the bar up by bending your elbows until you get a strong squeeze in your biceps. Lower slowly until your arms are straight again
cues: Avoid swinging your body, leaning back, or letting your elbows drift forward to make the weight easier.

name: Farmer's Carry/Walk
equipment: heavy dumbbells, kettlebells, or trap bar
steps: Pick up heavy dumbbells, kettlebells, or a trap bar; stand tall with shoulders down and back, core tight, and ribs stacked over hips.
Walk with controlled steps and weights steady by the sides; avoid shrugging or torso lean, keep breathing, and maintain a strong grip.

name: Flat Dumbbell Press
steps: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with dumbbells, kick them up one at a time while lying back, set arms over shoulders, retract and depress shoulder blades, and plant feet.
Brace the core and lower with elbows about 45–60 degrees from the torso, naturally turning hands slightly until weights reach torso level or a comfortable depth.
Press through the chest until arms are locked out over the shoulders, thinking of bringing the arms together.

name: Flat Machine Chest Press
steps: Set the seat so the handles are at a suitable level, keep the upper body about 60–70 degrees upright, use a shoulder-width grip, plant feet, and retract/depress the shoulder blades.

Press hands slightly inward to the start with elbows at the sides and roughly 60 degrees from the torso; brace and press until arms nearly lock out, thinking of bringing arms together, then control the return.

name: Flat Smith Machine Chest Press
steps: Place flat bench under bar, set starting rack so elbows are slightly bent, use medium slightly-wider-than-shoulder grip, retract/depress shoulders, plant feet, and unlock bar.
Lower to sternum with elbows about 60 degrees from torso, then press up/back to locked arms while thinking of drawing arms together.
cues: Refer to tutorial for Smith-specific setup details.

name: Forearm Push-Ups
steps: Adjust a bench to about a 60-degree incline, or any angle that allows you to comfortably lean your body weight against it. Place one hand flat against the bench with your arm fully extended and your fingers spread wide.

Push through your fingertips until you rise onto your fingers at the top of the movement. Slowly lower yourself back down in a controlled motion until your palm is flat against the bench again. You should feel most of the engagement in your forearms. Repeat for your desired number of reps.
cues: To make the exercise more challenging, lower the angle of the bench to increase resistance or wear a weighted vest for added intensity.

name: Forward Leg Swings
steps: Keep your core tight and hold onto something beside you. Swing your leg front and back as far as your leg will go. Repeat on the other side.
cues: This exercise is used to mobilize and warm up the hips and leg muscles for your leg movements.
tips: This exercise is used to mobilize and warm up the hips and leg muscles for your leg movements.

name: Front Foot Elevated Reverse Lunges
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand with your feet together on a small elevated platform like a weight plate. Brace your core.

While keeping your front leg planted on the platform, take a long step backwards with your other leg and sink down into a lunge position by driving the knee of your back leg towards the ground. Keep your back neutral and lean your torso forward slightly by about 20 degrees to better engage the glutes. Continue descending until your back knee almost touches the ground. Pause briefly in this position, and then push through the heel of your front leg to drive your hips forward, raising your body up back into the starting position with your feet together. Take your next step back with the other leg and continue alternating until you finish the desired number of reps on each leg.
cues: Avoid relying too much on your back leg to push your body up. Instead, after taking your step back, think of your back leg as a kickstand for balance and don’t rely on it too much to kick yourself back up.

name: Front Raises
steps: Begin with one dumbbell in one hand with your palms facing towards you in a standing position. Squeeze your glutes, flex your quads, and brace your core.

Take a deep breath in through your nose and then exhale as you raise your arm straight out in front of you and drive the dumbbell to shoulder height. Keep the movement nice and controlled without using momentum.
Slowly lower the weight back down to the starting position and repeat.

name: Front Squat
steps: Position the barbell across your front delts, and use a cross-arm grip with your elbows high and forward. If you have the mobility for it, you could also try a clean grip with your finger tips under the bar.

Unrack the bar, take a couple steps back, and position your feet just outside of shoulder-width with your toes slightly pointed out. Brace your core and lower yourself straight down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor. Keep your torso upright and keep your elbows high to prevent the bar from falling forward.
Drive back up while keeping your chest up and core engaged.

name: Glute Bridges
steps: Lay on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Engage your core to flatten your lower back against the floor.
Squeeze your butt muscles hard, and then lift your hips up while keeping your glutes contracted.

At the top, avoid arching your back. Instead, keep your core engaged and tilt your hips back by squeezing your glutes hard as if you had a 100 dollar bill between them and you were trying to prevent it from falling out. Hold this for 5 seconds before coming down for another rep.
cues: To make this move more difficult overtime and to help correct any strength imbalances you may have in your glutes, you can progress to working one leg at a time.

name: Glute Focused Leg Press
steps: Move the backrest to the lowest setting or just 1 to 2 notches up from the bottom. Adjust the foot plate starting position so that you only need to extend your legs slightly to be able to release the weights. Lastly, if your leg press has safety pins, adjust them so that they will be able to catch the weight at the bottom position if you are unable to lift it. It’s time to set your feet. Plant your feet relatively high on the footplate, around the middle of it or above. You’ll want to use a stance that’s about shoulder-width apart with your toes pointed out at about 15 degrees.

Unlock the safety pins, extend your legs to release the weights, and brace your core. From here, lower the weight by bending your legs. Continue lowering until your knees make a 90 degree angle. At this point, your shins should be straight on top of your feet. Push through your heels to push the weight back up. Continue pushing until your legs are almost fully straightened, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid letting your butt come up off the seat and lower back round at the bottom position. Instead, keep your core engaged, lower back flat against the pad, and butt in the seat. If needed, shorten the range of motion by not going as low to prevent this from happening. If possible, you can also try lowering the back rest even more and see if that helps.

name: Glute Ham Raise
steps: Set up the footplate such that your feet can lay flat and your knees are positioned just behind the pad when in the starting position. The closer to the thigh pad you adjust the footplate the harder the exercise will be, so if you're having a hard time, move the footplate further away.

Brace your core and slowly lower your body in a controlled movement. Your knees should gradually straighten while keeping your head, back and hips inline. Descend until you're either parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Ascend by contracting your hamstrings and glutes by bending at the knees while keeping your upper body in a straight line. Your upper body should move as one unit.
cues: Avoid excessive arching or rounding of the back. If you're feeling more of the movement in your lower back, then this is an indication that you should regress the exercise by adjusting the footplate or choosing an alternative.

name: Glute-Focused Step Downs
steps: Use a bench/box and light balance support; choose height that puts front thigh parallel at bottom.
Hinge hips back and lightly tap rear leg, then drive hips forward through planted-leg glute; hold a dumbbell opposite working leg to progress.
cues: Keep knee stacked over foot rather than driving it past toes for glute emphasis.

name: Goblet Squat (*lower back friendly)
steps: Grab a light kettlebell or dumbbell and hold it with an underhand grip tight at your chest. Then, set your feet. The optimal foot stance will vary for everyone, so experiment with a stance that is just outside shoulder-width with your toes pointed outwards at about 15 degree angle.

Brace your core. Keep the weight tight at your chest and squat straight down by bending at your hips and knees. As you do so, your bodyweight should be evenly distributed between your big toe, your little toe, and your heels. Your knees should also be bending slightly outwards in the same direction of your toes. Continue squatting down until your thighs reach at least parallel or slightly below.

From here, reverse the movement by extending your legs, thinking about bringing your upper back up towards the ceiling and exhaling as you do so. If you find it difficult to reach full depth, try elevating your heels onto weight plates to see if that helps.

name: Hack Squat Machine
steps: Set the machine with an even amount of weight on each side, and start out with a light weight to feel out the form. Grab the handles and set your shoulders up underneath the pad.

It’s time to set your feet. Generally you want a foot stance that is about shoulder-width apart or just wider than that, with your toes pointed out about 15 degrees. Do a few reps with some light weight to see how it feels and adjust your setup as needed. You should be able to reach the bottom position without your heels rising up.

Unlock the safety pins and extend your legs to release the weights. Brace your core and take a deep breath in through your nose. Lower the machine by leaning back into the pad and bending your legs and letting your knees bend slightly outwards over your toes. Go as deep as possible. Once you’ve reached the bottom position, keep your core braced and exhale as you push the weight back up until your legs are almost fully straight, and then descend into your next rep.

name: Half Kneeling Landmine Press (*shoulder friendly)
steps: Set a weighted barbell in a landmine; half-kneel a couple feet in front, with front leg planted and working-side leg behind, holding bar end at bottom a few inches in front of shoulder.
Squeeze glutes and brace, press toward ceiling to a straight arm, lower, then switch sides and legs after finishing one side.
cues: Keep torso stable and avoid twisting or using momentum.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Row
steps: Take a half kneeling stance in front of a cable machine with a handle attachment. The pulley height should be set so that when your arm is straight with the handle in your hand, the direction of the cable is in line with your arm at shoulder height. Grab the handle with your opposite arm, so that if your left leg is in front then your right arm will be pulling. Keep your back straight and brace your core.

As you pull, press the foot of your front down and forward into the ground, and then pull the elbow of your working arm down and back towards your sides. As you pull, keep your elbow tucked close to your side to better engage the lats. Stop once your elbow reaches your torso, control the weight back until your arm is almost fully straightened, and then repeat for another rep. Complete your reps on one side before switching to the other side.
cues: Avoid arching your lower back as you pull. Instead, keep your core engaged and back neutral. Avoid rotating your torso excessively as you pull. Instead, try to keep it facing forward and let all the movement come from your working arm.

name: Half-way Push-up Isometric
steps: Lower your body until you are in the middle of a push-up position.
Maintain and hold this position for 30 seconds.
cues: Ensure that any pain experienced during the hold does not exceed a level of three or four out of 10.

name: Hammer Curls
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand with your arms straight down by your sides.

Brace your core, and then while keeping a neutral grip on the dumbbell as if you were holding a hammer, curl your hand up and slightly in across your chest one arm at a time. You’ll alternate between arms each rep. As you curl, keep your elbow locked in place and control the weight all the way up and all the way down until your arm fully straightens. Keep your hand in the neutral grip throughout.

name: Hanging Leg Raises
steps: Hang off a bar with a wide overhand grip and your feet together. Engage your abs.

Curl your hips up towards your chest as far as you can. You’ll want to aim to get your knees up to the level of your shoulders. Then use your abs to control your hips back down to the starting position and then repeat for more reps.
cues: This is quite a difficult exercise, so to make it easier start out by performing it with your knees bent and kept close to your body. Then, as you get stronger, focus on straightening your legs a bit more and raising your hips higher and higher on the way up. Once you can do 3 sets of 15 reps with good form, you can then consider adding weight by holding a weighted ball or dumbbell between your feet.

name: Heavy Bench Press Isometric
steps: Use a load heavy enough that it cannot be moved and push against it for 30 seconds.
Keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce pushing intensity if pain exceeds 4/10.

name: Heavy Chest Machine Isometric
steps: Select machine weight heavy enough not to move and push against it while holding tension for 30 seconds.
Keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce pushing intensity if pain exceeds 4/10.

name: Heel Elevated Goblet Squat
steps: Grab a light kettlebell or dumbbell and hold it with an underhand grip tight at your chest. Then, set your feet. The optimal foot stance will vary for everyone, but I’d suggest first experimenting with a stance that is just outside shoulder-width with your toes pointed outwards at about 15 degree angle. Then place your heels up onto two 5 or 10lb weight plates.

Brace your core. Keep the weight tight at your chest and squat straight down by bending at your hips and knees. As you do so, drive your knees outwards in the same direction of your toes. Continue squatting down until your thighs reach at least parallel or slightly below. From here, reverse the movement by extending your legs, thinking about bringing your upper back up towards the ceiling and exhaling as you do so.
cues: Avoid letting the weight come up off your chest and leaning your chest forward. Instead, keep the weight tight to your chest thinking about squeezing it together, and then driving your chest up out of the bottom position. Avoid letting your knees cave in as you lift up. Instead, keep your knees inline with your toes throughout the movement.

name: Heel Elevated Split Squat
steps: Put working heel on 5–10 lb plate, hold dumbbells at sides, and use a hip-width split stance.
Brace, descend down/slightly forward with front knee toward toes until rear knee nearly touches floor, then extend front leg; finish one leg, rest one minute, then switch.
cues: Use back leg only as balance kickstand, with 80–90% load on front leg.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
steps: Set pads close together with outer thighs on pads; sit upright with a slight rear lean and hips slightly forward.
Hold handles if present, exhale and push thighs outward, then return under control.
A slight rear lean then a forward torso angle can emphasize different glute areas; use the positions that create best glute engagement.
cues: Avoid momentum and lumbar extension; brace and control each repetition.

name: Hip Adduction Machine
steps: Adjust the pads wide enough so that you feel a slight stretch in your inner thighs. If your legs are tight, it’s normal for it to be tricky to get into the machine, so put one leg in at a time and remember you can always widen it more overtime as you gain more mobility. Once you’re in, set up in an upright position with your back against the pad.

Grip the handles for support if your machine has them, then brace your core and exhale as you squeeze your thighs together until the pads lightly touch together. Slowly resist as the pads return to the starting position.
cues: Avoid using momentum and avoid letting your lower back arch. Keep your core engaged and control each rep.

name: Hip Thrust Machine
steps: Setup Lay on the machine with your hips and butt on the pad. Strap yourself in as snug as you can. Set your feet a little wider than hip width apart and toes pointed out slightly. Place them far enough from your body so that at the top position, are shins are almost vertical with your knees lined up above your feet.

Grip the handles, unrack the weight, and brace your core as if someone was about to punch your stomach. Press the handles forward with your arms to stabilize your upper body. Squeeze your glutes and then drive your hips towards the ceiling, pressing through the heels of your feet.
Keep going until your body is parallel to the ground. At this point, there should be a straight line with your torso and knees. Control the weight back down and then drive up for more reps.
cues: If you feel this more in your quads, you might need to move your feet further away from your body. If you feel this more in your hamstrings, you might need to move your feet closer towards your body. If you feel this more in your lower back, you need to engage your core more and focus on squeezing the glutes throughout the whole movement.

name: Hip Thrust Machine (Rest-Pause)

name: Hyperextensions (back/hamstring focused)
steps: Set thigh pads just below hip crease, plant heels on foot pad with slight toe turnout, cross hands over chest, and start torso slightly below parallel with straight back.
Tuck chin, brace, extend torso until aligned with lower body or slightly past, pause briefly, and return under control.
cues: After bodyweight mastery, load with a light/wide-grip barbell or dumbbells/plates while keeping core braced and shoulders set.

name: Hyperextensions (back/hamstring focused) (Rest-Pause)
steps: Using a back extension machine, adjust the thigh pads so that when you lay on it, the top of the pads are just below the crease of your hips. Position your heels firmly against the foot pad and keep them planted as you perform the movement with your toes slightly pointed out. Cross your hands over your chest and move your torso to the starting position slightly below parallel to the ground with your back straight.

Tuck your chin to align your neck with your spine and brace your core. From here, lift your chest up to extend your upper back. Continue until your torso is in line with your lower body, or just slightly past it. Pause here for a second, and then reverse the motion to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Once you master the exercise without weight, you can load it. One option is to use a barbell either empty or with light weight. Grab the bar with a wider overhand grip about 1.5x shoulder width, and get into the starting position. Before lifting up, brace your core, pinch your shoulder blades back together, and then pull your shoulders down and away from your ears. From here, perform the same movement. Another option is to hold a dumbbell or weight plates in each arm with your arms straight. Choose what is most comfortable and convenient for you.

name: Hyperextensions (Glute Focused)
steps: Using a back extension machine, adjust the thigh pads so that when you lay on it, the top of the pads are just below the crease of your hips. Position your heels firmly against the foot pad and keep them planted as you perform the movement with your toes pointed out just slightly. Cross your hands over your chest and move your torso to the starting position slightly below parallel to the ground with your back straight or just slightly rounded over.

Tuck your chin and brace your core. Squeeze your glutes together and think about driving your hips forward into the pad to lift your body up. Continue until your torso is in line with your lower body. Pause here for a second, and then reverse the motion by controlling your body back down to the starting position and repeat.
Once you master that without weight, you can load the exercise with using a barbell, dumbbell, or with weighted plates.
cues: To better engage the glutes, you can imagine there’s two dots at the top and bottom of your butt. As you perform the movement, you want to bring those two dots together by squeezing your glutes in order to lift your body up.

name: Incline Barbell Skullcrushers
steps: Set up an adjustable bench to an incline of about 45 degrees, which is typically 2-3 notches up from the bottom position. Grab a weighted bar or barbell with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart. Lay your back onto the bench and press the weight up so your arms are straight directly over your shoulders. Brace your core, flatten your lower back against the bench, and then while keeping your arms straight, move them back until they are parallel with your torso and lock them in this position.

Keep your elbows locked where they are, and then bend your forearms back behind your head as far as you can. Extend your forearms straight to get back into the starting position and then repeat for more reps.
cues: This exercise can be quite stressful on the elbows especially if done consistently over time. If you experience excessive elbow pain, or if you’ve used this exercise consistently for more than 8 weeks or so, then I’d suggest switching this out for an elbow friendly alternative such as the cable alternatives we’ve listed out.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curls
steps: Set up an incline bench to just a slight angle back of about 60 degrees, which is typically 2 to 3 notches down from the top position. Grab a pair of dumbbells and lay your back on the bench with your arms hanging straight down by your sides with your palms facing in and your feet planted firmly on the ground.

Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. While keeping both of your elbows locked into place, curl the weight up towards your shoulders. As you do so, rotate your palms so that they face up towards the ceiling at the top position. Lower the weight back down to the starting position letting your wrists rotate back into a neutral position. Once your arms fully straighten, repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid swinging your elbows forward and back excessively as you curl. Instead, keep your elbow locked in place. A little bit of movement is fine, but it shouldn’t be excessive. Avoid cutting the reps short by failing to fully extend your arm at the bottom position. Instead, fully extend your arm before initiating the next rep.

name: Incline Dumbbell Overhead Extensions
steps: Set up an adjustable bench to an incline of about 45 degrees, which is typically 2-3 notches up from the bottom position. Grab a pair of dumbbells and lay your back onto the bench with your arms straight over your shoulders and palms facing in towards each other. Brace your core, flatten your lower back against the bench, and then while keeping your arms straight, move them back until they are parallel with your torso and lock them in this position.

Keep your elbows locked and then bend your forearms back behind your head as far as you can. Extend your forearms straight without moving your elbows to get back into the starting position and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Keep the elbows fixed and move only the forearms during each repetition.

name: Incline Dumbbell Overhead Extensions (Rest-Pause)
steps: Set up an adjustable bench to an incline of about 45 degrees, which is typically 2-3 notches up from the bottom position. Grab a pair of dumbbells and lay your back onto the bench with your arms straight over your shoulders and palms facing in towards each other. Brace your core, flatten your lower back against the bench, and then while keeping your arms straight, move them back until they are parallel with your torso and lock them in this position.

Keep your elbows locked and then bend your forearms back behind your head as far as you can. Extend your forearms straight without moving your elbows to get back into the starting position and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Avoid swaying your elbows back and forth excessively as you perform each rep. Instead, keep your elbows locked in place and only move your forearms down and back up.

name: Incline Hammer Preacher Curl
steps: Set an incline bench with a preacher style pad or use a preacher bench set at an incline. Hold dumbbells with a neutral grip, thumbs up. Rest your upper arms on the pad.
Curl the dumbbells up without letting your upper arms lift off the pad. Squeeze near the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch. Keep your wrists neutral and avoid bouncing at the bottom.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
steps: Find your ideal seat height. Bring your elbows up to about a 45 to 60 degree angle from your body. Wherever your hands end up is the level you want the handles to be, so adjust your seat until you get that right. Use a relatively narrower grip just slightly outside of shoulderwidth. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and pinch them together.

Push the handles slightly into the starting position such that your elbows are by your sides and are tucked at roughly a 45 to 60 degree angle from your torso. Brace your core and push the handles until your arms fully lockout. Think about pulling your arms together as if you were trying to touch your biceps together to move the weight up. Control the weight back down to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Do not travel so far back that chest tension is lost; stop around elbow-at-torso level.

name: Incline Push-Ups (bands optional)
steps: Cross the band over once and loop your arm into each hole as if you were putting on a backpack. When done properly, it should make an X shape on your back. Hook each band with your thumbs. From here, find an elevated platform like a bench or a pair of two stable dumbbells. Using a grip just slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, get into a push-up position with your arms fully extended with the band in each hand and legs straight with toes together.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears, brace your core, and flex your thighs and glutes. Maintain this position as you slowly lower your body down by bending your elbows to about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your torso. Continue until your chest almost touches the bench or platform.
Then push up and back until your arms fully straighten. Let your shoulder-blades open up at the top before proceeding to the next rep.
cues: You can progress this by either lowering the platform, using a thicker band, or you can increase the number of reps you do all the way up to 30 reps per set.

name: (Bodyweight) Inner Chest Push-Up
steps: Get into a push-up position with one of your arms elevated on a stack of books or any elevated platform.
Perform a push-up, but as you press up, rotate your body towards the elevated arm so that your arm moves across your body more as you pushup.
Return back down to the bottom position of the push-up with your body straight. Repeat for the rest of your reps on that arm, and then switch to the other arm.
cues: Progression: You can start by doing these on your knees and then progress them by wearing a weighted bag

name: Inverted Row
steps: Set the bar to the appropriate height in the squat rack. The higher the bar the easier it’ll be, so I’d suggest starting out with it set at about chest height. Grab the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Move under the bar with your arms fully straight and legs fully extended in front of you with your toes together.

Brace your core and then lightly flex your quads and glutes. Then, while maintaining this position, pull your elbows back to lift yourself towards the bar. Continue pulling until your chest almost touches the bar. As you do so, your elbows should be angled at about a 60 degree angle away from your body. Control your body back down to the starting position with your arms fully straight, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Once you can do 3 sets of 10 reps in a row, you can lower the bar so that your body is more horizontal. Continue to repeat this process. Once you’re able to do this with your body almost completely horizontal to the ground is when you’re ready to progress to banded pull-ups or unassisted pull-ups.

name: JM Press
steps: This exercise will be used to target the triceps, mainly the lateral and medial heads, and will also help with improving bench press strength.
To perform it, lower the dumbbells down towards your neck while sliding your elbows forward.
You want as much elbow bend as possible, such that your forearm is parallel with the ground at the bottom. You can let them angle out on the way down if it’s more comfy on your elbows.
Then, simply use your triceps to extend your arms back up.
You can think of the exercise as if skullcrushers and close grip dumbbell press had a baby.
cues: Make sure to use lighter weight to avoid aggravating your elbows.

name: Kettlebell Swing
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder width and the kettlebell a short distance in front of you. Hinge at the hips and grab the bell with both hands. Keep your back flat and core tight.

Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to swing it up to about chest height. The power comes from your hips and glutes, not your arms. Let it swing back down and repeat smoothly. Avoid squatting the movement and avoid leaning back at the top.

name: Kneeling Lat Pulldowns
steps: Set high pulley with lat-pulldown attachment, grip just outside shoulders overhand, and kneel facing pulley.
Brace and slightly lean back; pull elbows down/back toward butt until bar reaches chin/below, then control up to nearly straight arms.
cues: If load pulls you off floor, it may be time to progress to inverted rows/pull-up negatives or banded pull-ups.

name: Kneeling One Arm Lat Pulldown
steps: Set a handle 2–3 notches below top, use a mat a few feet from pulley, and take a half-kneeling stance with the opposite leg forward; align straight arm about 45 degrees in front with cable in line with forearm.
Brace, pull elbow down and close to side, then toward spine at the end; pause, return to start, and complete one side before switching.
cues: Keep the elbow close to the body rather than flaring it to the side.

name: Lat Focused Cable Row
steps: Once you’ve found the right attachment, get into the starting position with your knees slightly bent on the pad.

Before pulling, brace your core and bring your shoulders down and away from your ears. Lean your torso forward over just slightly. Then, pull your elbows down and back towards your back pockets. As you pull, keep your elbow tucked close to your sides to better engage the lats. Stop when your elbows reach the level of your torso, and then control the weight back until your arms almost fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Keep torso slightly forward and stop when elbows reach torso; avoid leaning back or pulling elbows past torso.

name: Lat Focused Cable Row (Rest-Pause)
steps: Once you’ve found the right attachment, get into the starting position with your knees slightly bent on the pad.

Before pulling, brace your core and bring your shoulders down and away from your ears. Lean your torso forward over just slightly. Then, pull your elbows down and back towards your back pockets. As you pull, keep your elbow tucked close to your sides to better engage the lats. Stop when your elbows reach the level of your torso, and then control the weight back until your arms almost fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid leaning back and avoid pulling your elbows past your torso on the way back. Instead, to best engage the lats, try to keep your torso just slightly bent forward and stop each rep when your elbow reaches your torso.
tips: Avoid leaning back and avoid pulling your elbows past your torso on the way back. Instead, to best engage the lats, try to keep your torso just slightly bent forward and stop each rep when your elbow reaches your torso.

name: Lat Pulldowns
steps: Lock thighs under pads with feet flat; use overhand grip just outside shoulders and lean upper back slightly back.
Pull elbows until bar reaches chin, then control upward until arms are nearly extended.
cues: Use a thumbless grip and pull with elbows rather than hands.

name: Lat Pulldowns (Rest-Pause)
steps: Adjust the height of the seat or knee pads so that your thighs are securely locked underneath, with your feet flat on the floor. Set your weight then stand up and grab the bar with an overhand grip just outside shoulder-width apart. Sit back down with your thighs under the pads. Tilt your upper back just slightly backwards.
Pull your elbows down until the bar reaches the level of your chin. Control the weight back up until your arms are almost fully straight, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: To better engage the back muscles, you can try using a thumbless grip and think about pulling with the elbows rather than with your hands.
tips: To better engage the back muscles, you can try using a thumbless grip and think about pulling with the elbows rather than with your hands.

name: Lateral Band Walk
steps: Stand and place the mini band around your knees or ankles. Around the ankles will be harder. Get into an athletic stance with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent.

Take a small (6 inch) lateral step with one leg, then follow with another small step with the other leg. Repeat this series of small steps while keeping constant tension in the band. Then repeat again in the opposite direction.

Ensure that your upper body does not sway as you perform this movement. Keep your core tight, upper body facing straight and take each step in a controlled manner. You should feel a strong contraction in the side of your hip if done properly.

name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
steps: Set the seat so the pads sit on the outside of your upper arms, just above the elbows. Sit tall with your chest up, shoulders down, and core tight.
Raise your arms out to the sides until your upper arms are about level with your shoulders, then lower slowly. Keep the movement smooth and controlled, and avoid using momentum.
cues: If you feel it mostly in your traps (upper neck area), lighten the weight and focus on keeping shoulders down.

name: Lateral Raise Wall Push Isometric
steps: Stand sideways next to a wall.2
Press the outside of your upper arm into the wall.
Simulate the motion of a lateral raise without actually moving your arm.
Hold this position for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain level; it should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: If the pain level is higher than a four, reduce the intensity of your push against the wall.

name: Lean In Lateral Raise
steps: Grab a light dumbbell with one hand. Find a pole, wall, or any fixture to lean on, and lean your torso at about a 30 degree angle with your feet together and weighted arm in front of your torso. Another option is to set up sideways on an inclined bench.

While maintaining this position, raise your arm at a slight diagonal in front of you until your arm is fully straight on top of you. Keep your arm just slightly bent as you do so. Lower the weight back down until your hand reaches in front of your torso, then repeat for more reps. Finish one side and then switch to the other side.
cues: Note that this exercise does not require a lot of weight, so if you don’t have light enough dumbbells, you can try holding onto a 2.5 or 5 lb weight plate instead.

name: Leg Extensions Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use for standard repetitions.
Lift the weight to the middle position and hold it steady for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels throughout the exercise; the intensity should remain at or below a three or four out of 10.
cues: Reduce the weight if the pain level exceeds a four out of 10.

name: Leg Press Calf Raises
steps: With footplate unlocked and knees slightly bent, place balls of feet at the lower footplate edge using hip-width, toes-forward stance.
Rise through big toes, then lower slowly below the footplate for a calf stretch, pause, and repeat.

name: Leg Press Calf Raises (Rest-Pause)
steps: Get your legs into the starting position with the footplate unlocked and your legs slightly bent. Move the balls of your feet down towards the bottom of the footplate so that the rest of your foot hangs off the edge. Use a hip-width stance with your toes facing forward.

Push up onto your toes as high as you can, keeping the weight on your big toes. Once you reach the top position, slowly lower the weight back down until your heel extends below the foot plate to fully stretch your calf. Pause at the bottom briefly, and then push up for another rep.

name: Light Bench Press Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use.
Lower the weight to the middle position of the bench press.
Hold this middle position for 30 seconds.
Monitor your discomfort levels. The intensity should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: Reduce the weight if your pain exceeds a level of four out of 10.

name: Light Lateral Raise Isometric
steps: Use a weight that is lighter than what you would typically use for a standard lateral raise.
Raise the weight to the middle position and hold it there.
Maintain this hold for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels during the exercise.
The pain intensity should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: If your discomfort level is higher than this, decrease the weight.

name: Light Overhead Press Isometric
steps: Choose a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use.
Move the weight to the middle position of an overhead press and hold it there.1
Maintain this isometric hold for 30 seconds.
Ensure your pain level does not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: If the pain level surpasses a four out of 10, reduce the weight being used.

name: Low Incline Barbell Press
steps: Set bench to roughly 15–30 degrees; arrange rack so bar meets mid-chest at the bottom; grip slightly outside shoulder width and set shoulder blades down/back with feet firmly planted.
Lower with elbows roughly 45–60 degrees from torso until bar is about an inch above mid-chest; press up and slightly back to locked arms over shoulders.
cues: If using a pre-set bench that cannot be adjusted, swap to Low Incline Dumbbell Press; fixed benches may overemphasize front delts.

name: Low Incline Cable Press
steps: Place the incline bench over to the middle of a cable machine with the pulleys set to the lowest position with a handle attachment in each. Position the bench such that when you lay on the bench and tuck your elbows to about a 45 to 60 degree angle, the handles are lined up directly inline with your hands. Then, grab each handle, sit on the bench, and tuck your elbows to about a 60 degree angle from your body. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and pinch them together.

Brace your core and begin your first rep by pushing the handles up and then back until your arms are fully extended above the level of your shoulders. To better engage the chest, think about trying to squeeze your biceps into the sides of your chest until your arms straighten. Control the weight back down to the starting position and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Avoid going too low during each rep. This no longer engages the chest and can be harmful on the shoulders. Instead, stop each rep when your hands reach about an inch above the level of your chest.

name: Low Incline Dumbbell Press
steps: Set bench 15–30 degrees, kick dumbbells into position, set scapulae, maintain a small lumbar arch, and plant feet.
Brace, lower with controlled elbow angle, then press while maintaining upper-body position.
cues: Keep chest up and scapulae back/down; do not round shoulders or flare elbows. Keep elbows around 45–60 degrees from torso.

name: Low Incline Smith Machine Press
steps: Place an incline bench beneath the bar of the smith machine and set it up to about 15 to 30 degrees. This is typically just one notch up from the bottom position. Rack the bar into its starting position such that when you grab the bar, your elbows are just slightly bent. Grip the bar just slightly outside shoulder-width apart. Before unracking, set your back by pulling your shoulder blades down and back to create a little bit of space between your lower back and the bench. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Unrack the bar by lifting it up slightly and twisting the bar to get it into the unlocked position.

Control the weight down by dropping your elbows down at about a 45 to 60 degree angle from your torso. Stop when the bar reaches about an inch or so above the level of your mid-chest. Then, push the bar up and back to the starting position with your arms fully locked out. Think about pulling your arms together as if you were trying to touch your biceps together to move the weight up.
cues: Avoid letting your wrists bend as you press. Instead, think about punching the ceiling with the bar to keep your wrists stacked vertically. Avoid letting your shoulders round forward at the top position. Instead, keep your chest up and out and shoulder blades back and down.

name: Low to High Cable Fly
steps: Take both cable handles with neutral grip, step forward, and use a stable split stance that produces a full stretch.
Draw cables up and across to meet in middle of chest, then control them back and repeat.

name: LU Raises
steps: Stand tall with a light dumbbell or small plate in each hand and brace your core.
Raise the weights directly out to the sides in a controlled motion, then lower them under control.
cues: Use a very light dumbbell or plate, brace before lifting, and raise directly to the side.

name: Lying Dumbbell Curls
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and set yourself up sideways against a flat bench with your upper back and upper arms resting on the pad.

Use your glutes to support your body up, and let your arms hang down by your sides. Brace your core, and then curl the dumbbells up. As you do so, keep your elbows locked in place and don’t let your upper arms come off the pad. Slowly control the weight back down until your arms are fully straight, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Your biceps may not be used to this level of stretch, so start light and go heavier as you get more comfortable with the exercise.

name: Lying Incline Lateral Raise
steps: Set up an incline bench to roughly a 45 degree angle, which is typically 2 to 3 notches up from the bottom of a bench. Grab a pair of light dumbbells. Lay your chest on the bench with your legs straight for support and your arms hanging by your sides.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. From here, while keeping your arms just slightly bent, raise your hands out in front of you. As you do so, raise your arms in a Y position in front of you. This is about 15 to 30 degrees in front of your body. Raise the weight until your arms reach shoulder-height, control them back down to the starting position, and then repeat for more reps.
cues: Note that this exercise does not require a lot of weight, so if you don’t have light enough dumbbells, you can try holding onto a 2.5 or 5 lb weight plate instead. To better help with muscle activation, you can try using a thumbless grip if using dumbbells and rather than thinking about raising the weight up, think about raising the weight out as if you were pushing your hands out towards the walls.

name: Lying Leg Curls
steps: Set foot pad just above back of heel, align knee near machine pivot, and make setup adjustments to maintain position.
Brace abs, pull handles down with lats, point toes down, curl toward butt, then lower under control to almost-straight legs.
cues: Do not fully straighten legs at the bottom; stopping slightly short reduces calf involvement.

name: Lying Windshield Wipers
steps: Lay on your back with your legs raised and a slight bend in your knees. Hold a weight or backpack tight against your chest to help keep your upper body locked down against the ground. Brace your core and keep your lower back from arching as you get into position.

From here, slowly twist your legs down towards one side while keeping your shoulders and upper back planted on the ground. Continue until your feet almost touch the floor, then use your obliques to twist your legs back up and over to the other side. Repeat this side-to-side motion under control until you complete the desired number of reps on each side.

name: Meadows Row
steps: Stand sideways to a landmine or barbell secured in a corner. Stagger your stance with the foot closest to the bar planted behind you for balance and your other foot planted flat in front of you for support. Bend your knees and hinge at your hips, keeping your back flat, and grab the bar with an overhand grip while placing your other hand or elbow rest on your front leg for support.

Brace your core and think about driving your elbow back behind you, keeping your elbow angled out in an arrow shape. Pull back as far as you can, squeezing your shoulder blade in, then control the weight down slowly until your shoulder blade fully opens up at the bottom for a deep stretch. Complete the number of desired reps on one arm, rest for 30-60 seconds, then switch sides to work the other side.
As you pull, avoid rotating your torso. Keep your torso flat and lower back straight.
To better engage your back, think about pulling with your elbows rather than your hands.

I’d also recommend using smaller 10 or 25lb plates to load the bar so you can get as deep of a range of motion at the bottom as possible, or else the bigger plates will touch the floor before your arm can fully straighten
Lastly, consider using a wrist strap to make sure your grip doesn’t give out before your back muscles do.

name: Neutral Grip Dumbbell Press (*Shoulder Friendly)
steps: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with dumbbells, kick them up one at a time while lying back, place arms over shoulders with palms facing each other, retract/depress shoulder blades, and plant feet.
Brace and lower with elbows about 45 degrees from the torso until weights reach torso level or a comfortable depth.
Press through the chest until arms are locked out over the shoulders, thinking of bringing the arms together.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneel on a padded surface with your ankles secured under a sturdy support. Keep your hips extended so your body is a straight line from knees to head. Brace your core.
Slowly lean forward, resisting the fall with your hamstrings. Go as far as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands and push lightly off the floor to return to the start.
cues: Keep your hips from folding and avoid bending at the waist.

name: Overhead Extensions Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use.
Hold the movement in the middle position for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels; the pain should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: If your pain level is higher than a four out of 10, reduce the weight.

name: Overhead Rope Extensions (Rest-Pause)
steps: Use a rope attachment and pull it through so that you can grab just one end of it with the cable set at the lowest position. Grab your handle with one hand, face away from the cable, take one step forward and one step to the side of your working arm. Bring your arm over your head with your hand bent behind your head. Your arm should be up and facing slightly out.

While keeping your elbow locked in place, extend your hand out fully, keeping it in line with your arm. Lower back down to the starting position, and then repeat for more reps. Finish your reps on one side before switching to the other side.
cues: Avoid swaying your elbows back and forth excessively as you perform each rep. Instead, keep your elbows locked in place and only move your forearms down and back up. Avoid excessively arching your lower back and flaring your ribs out. Instead, keep your core engaged. Avoid cutting the range of motion short. Instead, lighten the weight and focus on bringing your hands all the way behind your head to get a full stretch on the triceps.
tips: Avoid swaying your elbows back and forth excessively as you perform each rep. Instead, keep your elbows locked in place and only move your forearms down and back up. Avoid excessively arching your lower back and flaring your ribs out. Instead, keep your core engaged. Avoid cutting the range of motion short. Instead, lighten the weight and focus on bringing your hands all the way behind your head to get a full stretch on the triceps.

name: Palloff Press
steps: Set the cable machine with a handle attachment to around the level of your chest. Position yourself sideways from the cable, grab the handle by interlocking both hands around it, and then take a few steps laterally away from it while keeping the handle at your chest. Maintain just a slight bend in your knees.

Brace your core, and then while keeping your body straight and hips facing forward, slowly extend your arms outward in front of you at the height of your chest. Continue until they’re completely straight and then slowly bring your arms back to the starting position before continuing for another rep. Continue your reps on one side before facing the other way to work the other side.
cues: If you’re using a band instead of a cable machine, you’ll simply loop it around a stable fixture at this height. Once this becomes easy, you can choose to either increase the weight, step further away from the cable or band, and/or introduce a squat to the movement by bending your knees a little bit more as you perform it, and gradually getting to the point where you’re able to do this in a full squat position.

name: Pec-Deck Machine Fly
steps: Set seat so arms sit just below shoulder height; use a slightly bent-arm start, high elbows, planted feet, and depressed/retracted scapulae.
Bring arms together with chest, pause, then slowly return until elbows are level with torso.
cues: Do not fully straighten arms at the start or over-bend them at the end; keep a controlled arm path to retain chest tension rather than shifting work to biceps.

name: Pec-Deck Machine Fly (Rest-Pause)
steps: Adjust the height of the seat such that when you grab the handles your arms are just below shoulder height. Grab each handle with your arms slightly bent and elbows kept high inline with the rest of your arm. Plant your feet firmly on the ground and move your butt about an inch or two forward on the seat. Pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears and pinch them together.

Use your chest to bring your arms together with your arms straight in front of you. Pause at the end position briefly, slowly control the weight back while bending your arms until your elbows reach the level of your torso, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid straightening your arms completely at the starting position and avoid bending your arms too much at the end position. This takes away tension from the chest and shifts more of the work to the biceps. Instead, keep your arms bent at the start and then straight at the end as if you were trying to touch your biceps together.
tips: Avoid straightening your arms completely at the starting position and avoid bending your arms too much at the end position. This takes away tension from the chest and shifts more of the work to the biceps. Instead, keep your arms bent at the start and then straight at the end as if you were trying to touch your biceps together.

name: Pendulum Squat
steps: Set up with back/hips supported, shoulder-width feet planted, and core braced.
Lower with stable back to near-parallel/deep range, then drive through midfoot/heel while knees track toes and hips stay on pad.

name: Pike Pushup
steps: From push-up position, walk hands toward feet with straight legs into an inverted V.
Lower nose near floor with head moving forward beyond hands; keep elbows tucked and forearms vertical, then extend arms back up.
cues: Progress knees → standard → elevated feet → hands closer to feet → higher feet elevation.

name: Pistol Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg held out in front. Keep your chest up, core tight, and your working foot flat.

Slowly squat down by sitting your hips back and bending the knee while keeping the knee tracking over the toes. Use your arms for balance. Go as low as you can without collapsing or letting the heel lift, then push through your foot to stand back up. If needed, start by doing them to a box or holding a support.

name: 3 Point Dumbbell Row
steps: Use a flat bench/elevated platform and one hand for support; take squat stance, tip to bench, hold dumbbell with other hand, and keep neutral back/head down.
Brace, row elbow back close to side, lower to start, and finish one side before switching.
cues: Keep hand directly below elbow to avoid shifting the work toward biceps.

name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)
steps: Set preacher bench so armpits rest on pad and upper arms are supported; start with nearly straight arms and relaxed shoulders.
Curl until forearms near vertical, then lower slowly to biceps stretch without hard lockout; keep upper arms on pad and do not bounce.

name: Preacher Curl (Machine)
steps: Set seat/chest and arm support so armpits sit at pad top; start nearly straight with shoulders down and elbows fixed.
Curl to near-vertical forearms, lower under control without lockout/slamming, and keep upper arms on pad.
cues: Keep upper arms glued to pad.

name: Preacher Curl Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would use for a normal workout.
Assume the preacher curl position and hold the weight in the middle of the range of motion.
Maintain this hold for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels during the hold. Your discomfort should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: Reduce the weight if the pain level exceeds a four out of 10.

name: Prone Arm Circles
steps: Lay on the floor or ideally on a flat bench with a light weight in each hand and your head extending off the end of the bench. First start out with 2.5 or 5lb weight plates in each hand, or even without any weight, to see if you have the strength needed to properly perform it.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Then with your palms facing downwards, raise your arms straight in front trying to get them to at least parallel with your torso. If you’re on the ground, then try to raise your arms so they are about an inch off the ground. From here, while keeping your arms straight, make a large circle with your arms while rotating your hands until your hands meet your butt. At this point your palms should now be facing the ceiling. From here, move your arms back to the starting position to complete 1 full rep, and then repeat.
cues: Avoid excessively arching the lower back and lifting your chest up too high. Instead, keep your core and glutes engaged to stabilize your body and try to keep your chest in contact with the ground or bench. Avoid rushing through the movement. Instead, control each rep and feel the muscles working.

name: (Weighted) Prone Arm Circles
steps: Lay on the floor or ideally on a flat bench with a light weight in each hand and your head extending off the end of the bench. First start out with 2.5 or 5lb weight plates in each hand, or even without any weight, to see if you have the strength needed to properly perform it.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Then with your palms facing downwards, raise your arms straight in front trying to get them to at least parallel with your torso. If you’re on the ground, then try to raise your arms so they are about an inch off the ground. From here, while keeping your arms straight, make a large circle with your arms while rotating your hands until your hands meet your butt. At this point your palms should now be facing the ceiling. From here, move your arms back to the starting position to complete 1 full rep, and then repeat.
cues: Avoid excessively arching the lower back and lifting your chest up too high. Instead, keep your core and glutes engaged to stabilize your body and try to keep your chest in contact with the ground or bench. Avoid rushing through the movement. Instead, control each rep and feel the muscles working.

name: Pull-Up Negatives
equipment: optional tall bench or elevated step
steps: If needed, place a tall bench/elevated step a couple of feet in front of the pull-up bar to help reach the top.
Use a wide overhand grip and the bench to kick to the top with the chin over the bar; keep the core engaged, depress the shoulder blades, and straighten the arms.
At the bottom, return feet to the bench and repeat; aim to lengthen the lowering phase to a five-second descent.

name: Pull-Ups
steps: Grip the bar using an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. From here, let your body hang and then begin stabilizing your body by bringing your feet together, flexing your quads and glutes and contracting your abs. You want to maintain this position as you pull.

Initiate the pull by first bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears. Then, pull your elbows down and back into your sides as if you were trying to pull them into your back pockets. As you do this, think about trying to bring your chest up towards the bar. Continue pulling-up until your chin is above the bar. From here, control yourself by letting your elbows move up and out until your arms are almost fully straightened, and then continue into your next rep.
cues: Use an overhand grip outside shoulder width and pull chin over bar; choose an alternative if six continuous reps are not achievable.

name: Pull-ups Isometric
steps: App panel states to begin a push-up movement and lower to its middle position.
Hold middle position 30 seconds.
cues: Keep discomfort at or below 3–4/10.

name: Pulldowns Isometric
steps: Select a weight that is lighter than what you would normally use.
Perform a pulldown and hold the middle position.
Maintain this isometric hold for 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels during the movement; it should not exceed a three or four on a scale of 10.
cues: Reduce the weight further if the pain level is higher than a three or four.

name: Push-Up Progression
steps: In this progression, we’ll cover 3 exercises you can use to gradually build up your strength to be able to do unassisted push-ups on your toes.
Push-Up Negatives (0:24)
This takes advantage of the fact that you have the strength required to lower yourself down into a push-up, but may not yet have the full strength to push your whole body up.

Get down on all fours and set your hands by placing them just slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Next, with your arms fully extended, extend your legs one at a time straight behind you with your toes together.

Stabilize your body by bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears, engaging your core as if someone were about to punch your stomach, and flexing your thighs and glutes. Then, tuck your chin to align your neck with your spine. Maintain this position as you lower your body down as slowly as you can by bending your elbows to the shape of an arrow, about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your torso. Continue lowering until your body reaches the ground. You should travel down and slightly forwards. Once you’re lying flat on the ground, keep your knees on the ground and keep your elbows tucked towards your sides in an arrow shape, and then push yourself back up until your arms fully straighten and shoulder-blades open up. Continue your next rep by repeating this process.
Once you’re able to do 3 sets of at least 5 reps with a 5 second descent is when you’re ready to move to the next progression.
Band Assisted Push-Up (2:12)
If you have a Built With Science band, use that, otherwise you can use another band. The thicker the band the easier it will be.

Double loop the band and then wrap it around your upper arms, just above the level of your elbows. Then, get into your push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, legs straight, and toes together.

Stabilize your body by bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears, engaging your core as if someone were about to punch your stomach, and flexing your thighs and glutes. At this point your body should make a straight line from your head to hips to toes. Maintain this position as you lower your body down as slowly as you can by bending your elbows to the shape of an arrow, about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your torso. Continue lowering until your chest almost touches the ground. You should travel down and slightly forwards and the band should stretch more and more as you lower down. From here, push up and back until your arms fully straighten. Once you can comfortably do 3 sets of that is when you’re ready to move onto progression 3.
Push-Ups (on toes) (3:43)

Get down on all fours and set your hands by placing them just slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Next, with your arms fully extended, extend your legs one at a time straight behind you with your toes together.

Stabilize your body by bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears, engaging your core as if someone were about to punch your stomach, and flexing your thighs and glutes. At this point your body should make a straight line from your head to hips to toes. Maintain this position as you lower your body down as slowly as you can by bending your elbows to the shape of an arrow, about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your torso. Continue lowering until your chest almost touches the ground. You should travel down and slightly forwards. From here, push up and back until your arms fully straighten. Let your shoulder-blades open up at the top before proceeding to the next rep.

Aim to do a total of 3 sets of 6-12 reps with good form. However, if you can’t quite do 6 reps yet, that’s perfectly fine. In this case, just try to do as many as you can each set without going to complete failure and while keeping proper form. A good option if you can’t do 6 reps is to perform your first set as full push-ups, and then for sets 2 and 3 use either progression 2 with the band or progression 1 push-up negatives since you’ll be able to do more reps with that and can continue building up your full push-up strength over time.

name: Push-Ups (bands optional)
steps: Optional band setup: cross the band once and loop arms through as a backpack, creating an X on the back and hooking each band with the thumbs; place hands just wider than shoulder width and extend legs behind with toes together.
Depress the shoulders, brace, flex thighs and glutes, tuck the chin, and lower with elbows 45–60 degrees from the torso until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Press up and back until arms are fully straight, allowing shoulder blades to open at the top before the next repetition.

name: Push-Ups (bands optional) (Rest-Pause)
steps: Optional band setup: cross the band once and loop arms through as a backpack, creating an X on the back and hooking each band with the thumbs; place hands just wider than shoulder width and extend legs behind with toes together.
Depress the shoulders, brace, flex thighs and glutes, tuck the chin, and lower with elbows 45–60 degrees from the torso until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Press up and back until arms are fully straight, allowing shoulder blades to open at the top before the next repetition.

name: Pushdown Isometric
steps: Use lighter-than-normal load with straight bar or rope, hold the pushdown at middle position for 30 seconds.
Keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce weight if pain surpasses 4/10.

name: Quad-Focused Leg Press
steps: Set backrest low, adjust start position/safety pins, set shoulder-width-or-wider stance with toes out, then unlock safety.
Brace, lower by bending knees slightly out over toes as deep as possible, then exhale and press to almost-straight legs.
cues: This guide is for the 45-degree plate-loaded leg press; use an alternative if only a horizontal leg press is available.

name: Rear Delt Cable Fly
steps: Set high cable pulleys without handles; cross the cables by holding left with right hand and right with left hand, step back, and bring straight arms forward at shoulder height.
Brace and pull straight arms down at 45 degrees from torso until slightly past it; pause, then control back to the start.
cues: For a one-arm version, stand sideways so the cable lines up with the arm, and pull the arm down at a 45-degree angle away from the body.

name: Rear Delt Cable Fly (Rest-Pause)
steps: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with the pulleys set at the highest height with no handles attached. Grab the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand. Grab the little ball at the end of the cable for grip. Step a few steps back, and then move your arms straight in front of you at shoulder height. At this point the cables should be crossing over each other. You can rotate your hands slightly outwards to match the direction of the cable.

Brace your core and pull your arms down at a 45 degree angle away from your torso while keeping your arms straight. Continue pulling as far back as you can so that your arms end up slightly past your torso. Pause at the end position briefly, and then control the weight back to the starting position with your arms straight in front of your chest.
cues: If you’re performing just one arm at a time, you’d perform it the exact same way, but just make sure that you position yourself so that when you pull your arm down, the cable is in line with your arm and that your arm makes a 45 degree angle away from your body. Standing directly sideways to the cable helps make this easy to set up.

name: Rear Delt Cable Row
steps: Once you’ve found the right attachment so that your hands are outside shoulder width apart, get into the starting position with your knees slightly bent on the pad.

Before pulling, brace your core and bring your shoulders down and away from your ears. Then, pull the weight towards your sternum, keeping your elbows out at about a 45 degree angle away from your torso. Pull your elbows as far back as you can behind your body. Control the weight back until your arms fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: To better engage the rear delts, think about pulling with your elbows rather than your hands.

name: Reverse Crunches
steps: Lay your back on the bench with your knees bent in the air at a 90 degree angle. To stabilize your body, grab under one end of the bench with your arms.

Engage your abs and tilt your pelvis forwards. Lift your hips up off the bench by thinking about curling your hips up towards your chest. Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position with your low back flat against the bench and then repeat for another rep.
cues: The more bent your knees and the closer they are to your body, the easier it will be. So try it out with your knees quite bent and then try extending them further away from your body to make it more difficult. Eventually you can start loading the exercise with weight by squeezing an exercise ball between your knees as you perform it. To best engage the lower abs, perform this exercise on a decline bench if you have one available.

name: Reverse Curls (Cables)
steps: Use a low cable with a straight bar. Grip it palms down about shoulder width. Stand tall with elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the bar up smoothly, then lower slowly back down. Keep wrists straight and avoid using your hips or shoulders to move the weight.

name: Reverse Curls (Dumbbell)
steps: Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing down. Keep elbows close to your sides and shoulders relaxed.
Curl the dumbbells up without swinging. Focus on lifting with your forearms and keeping wrists straight. Lower slowly to full arm extension. Avoid leaning back or letting elbows drift forward.

name: Reverse Lunges (*knee friendly)
steps: Hold dumbbells at sides, stand feet together, and brace.
Take a long reverse step, lower rear knee near floor with front shin nearly vertical, pause, then drive through front heel and hips forward to stand.
cues: A neutral-back forward torso lean during descent can better target glutes.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
steps: Set seat so arms are parallel to floor and use neutral grip.
Pull arms back with straight, locked elbows; squeeze shoulder blades and avoid upper-trap tension or shrugging.

name: Reverse Pec Deck (Rest-Pause)
steps: Adjust the seat height such that when you grab the handles, your arms are just about parallel with the floor. Use a neutral grip where the palms face each other to grab the handles.

Pull your arms back while keeping your arms straight and elbows locked throughout each rep. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together and avoid tensing up your upper traps or shrugging up your shoulders as you pull.

name: RKC Plank
steps: Get into a plank position with your elbows under your shoulders, legs straight, feet together, and head facing down. Your body should make a straight line.

While maintaining a plank position, contract your abs and squeeze your glutes hard Then pull your elbows down against the floor while pulling your toes up towards your head. Your elbows and toes won’t move, but pull them against the floor as if you were trying to slide them together. Continue holding this position for the designated amount of time.
cues: To increase the difficulty, in the starting position, move your elbows up towards the level of your head and repeat the same sequence we just went through.

name: Rope Cable Curls (*neutral grip)
steps: Set rope at lowest pulley, use neutral grip with arms straight in front of thighs.
Slightly flare and lock elbows, brace, curl rope to chest, then control down.

name: Rope Overhead Tricep Extensions
steps: Move the cable down to about hip height, and attach a rope to it. A double rope with the grip pulled through can be comfier on the elbows, but a single rope is perfectly fine as well if you don’t want to hog 2 ropes. Grab the ends of the rope with each hand then face away from the cable and squat down so that your hands are holding the rope behind your head. Squat up and keep your elbows straight up and tight together with your hands behind your neck.

Brace your core as if someone was about to punch your stomach, and then while keeping your elbows locked in place, extend your arms up and out until they are straight. Slowly lower them back to the starting position, getting a deep stretch in your triceps by letting your hands come back behind your neck as low as possible before starting your next rep.
cues: Avoid standing too far from the cable. Stand as close as possible to make the exercise more difficult when your triceps are stretched, which seems to be better for growth. Avoid arching your lower back, keep it flat by bracing your core. On the way down, avoid stopping half way. Go as deep as you comfortably can to maximize the stretch in your triceps.
