name: Russian Twists
steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and heels on the ground. Lean back slightly so your torso is at an angle and you feel your abs working. Keep your chest up and your back long, not rounded.

Clasp your hands or hold a weight close to your chest. Rotate your shoulders and ribcage to one side, then the other, moving as a unit. Keep your hips mostly still and avoid just swinging your arms. Move with control and keep breathing.

name: Seated Bodyweight Calf Raises
steps: While holding onto a stable fixture for support, get down into a squat position with your toes facing forward and feet set at about shoulder width apart. Let your heel come down towards the ground as far as they can.

Push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toe. Control your heel slowly back down towards the ground as far as they’ll go, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid mindlessly going through the reps and using momentum and gravity to bring you up and down. Instead, spend time controlling every single rep and feeling your calf contract then stretch.

name: Seated Bodyweight Calf Raises (Rest-Pause)
steps: While holding onto a stable fixture for support, get down into a squat position with your toes facing forward and feet set at about shoulder width apart. Let your heel come down towards the ground as far as they can.

name: Seated Cable Row (mid/upper back focused)
steps: Sit with slightly bent knees and straight back, brace, and depress shoulders.

Pull elbows behind body at 45–60 degrees while squeezing shoulder blades, then control forward; upper body may round forward to open upper back if core stays tight and low back does not round excessively.
cues: A wider handle that permits elbows to flare is preferred; a V-bar is acceptable if needed.

name: Seated Cable Row (mid/upper back focused) (Rest-Pause)
steps: Once you’ve found the attachment, get into the starting position with your knees slightly bent on the pad and back straight.
Brace your core and bring your shoulders down and away from your ears. Pull your elbows back behind your body at about a 45 to 60 degree angle away while squeezing your shoulder blades together.

Control the weight back down to the starting position, letting your shoulder blades open up, and then go into your next rep. You can let your upper body round forward to fully open up your back, as long as your core remains tight and your lower back doesn’t round excessively.
cues: You can use the V-bar attachment, but a better option would be a wider handle setup so that your elbows can flare outwards as you pull. If you don’t have access to any of that, you can try putting two handles over a lat pulldown attachment and twist them to lock them in place.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curls
steps: Sit upright on 90-degree incline bench with dumbbells at sides and feet under knees.
Depress shoulders/brace, curl one dumbbell while supinating palm upward, lower while returning to neutral wrist, and alternate starting with weaker arm.
cues: Keep elbows fixed and fully extend at bottom rather than cutting range short.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curls (Rest-Pause)
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on an incline bench with the backrest set at a 90 degree angle. Let your arms hang down by your sides and plant your feet firmly on the ground under your knees.

Bring your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. While keeping your elbow locked into place, with one arm curl the weight up towards your shoulders. As you do so, rotate your palms so that they face up towards the ceiling at the top position. Lower the weight back down to the starting position, letting your wrists rotate back into a neutral position, and then repeat with the other arm. Start each set with your weaker arm and continue alternating arms every rep until you complete the required number of reps for each arm.
cues: Avoid swinging your elbows forward and back excessively as you curl. Instead, keep your elbow locked in place. A little bit of movement is fine, but it shouldn’t be excessive. Avoid cutting the reps short by failing to fully extend your arm at the bottom position. Instead, fully extend your arm before initiating the next rep.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: Set bench 60–75 degrees, kick dumbbells over shoulders, plant feet, and set elbows slightly forward around 45 degrees.
Depress shoulders/brace, press dumbbells over shoulders to straight arms, then lower elbows about 45 degrees forward until weights reach chin level.

name: Seated Flat Cable Press
steps: Place an incline bench at about 75 degrees in cable middle, set cables at lower-chest height, set elbows 60 degrees, plant feet, and set scapulae.
Brace and press handles to lockout while thinking of drawing arms together; control back.
cues: Set cable height so forearms align perfectly with cable at both endpoints.

name: Seated Leg Curls
steps: Set up your back rest so that when you sit down, your knees are aligned directly beside the pivot point of the machine. For most people, your knees should end up just past the edge of the seat. Next, adjust the height of your foot pad so that when you’re seated, your legs are in just a slightly bent position. The pad should also be resting just above the back of your heels.

Grab the handles on the side of the machine and pull up on them by engaging your lats. Brace your core, and then while keeping your toes pointed straight up, pull the weight as far down as you can using your hamstrings. Slowly control the weight back close to the starting position with your legs almost fully extended, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid fully extending your legs at the top position. The first 15 degrees or so of the movement actually involves more of the calves, so cut the range of motion short slightly by stopping each rep a little before your legs are completely straightened at the top position.

name: Seated Leg Extensions
steps: Align knees with machine pivot and set foot pad just above ankles at about a 90-degree knee angle.
Hold handles, brace, keep toes up and knees facing forward, extend with quads, pause, then control the load to the start.
cues: Keep core braced and lumbar spine neutral; pull on handles to engage lats. Do not swing or drop the load—maintain quad tension with controlled repetitions.

name: Seated Leg Extensions (Rest-Pause)
steps: Set up your back rest so that when you sit down, your knees are aligned directly beside the pivot point of the machine. For most people, your knees should end up just past the edge of the seat. Next, adjust the height of your foot pad so that when you’re seated, your legs are at a roughly 90 degree angle with the pad resting just above your ankle.

Grab the handles on the side of the machine and pull up on them by engaging your lats. Brace your core, and then while keeping your toes pointed straight up, use your quads to extend your legs straight forward. As you do so, keep your knees facing forward rather than rotating them in or outwards. Extend as far up as you can, pause briefly at the top, and then control the weight all the way back down to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Avoid arching your lower back as you extend your legs up. Instead, keep your core braced, lower back neutral, and continue pulling up on the handles to keep your lat muscles engaged. Avoid swinging the weight up and letting gravity drop your legs back down. Instead, keep constant tension in your quads by controlling the weight up and then slowly lowering it back down.

name: Seated Mid-Chest Cable Fly
steps: Place an adjustable bench a couple feet in front of cable machine at about 75 degrees; set cables at mid-chest and hold handles with bent elbows and cable-aligned forearms.
Retract/depress shoulder blades, bring arms together with chest until straight in front, pause, then return while bending arms until elbows reach torso level.
cues: Keep arms bent at start and straight at end; excessive straightening at start or bending at end shifts work toward biceps.

name: Seated Mid-Chest Cable Fly (Rest-Pause)
steps: Move an adjustable bench over to the middle of a cable machine, positioned a couple of feet in front of it. Set the incline to one notch down from the highest position to about a 75 degree angle. Adjust the height of the cables around the level of your mid-chest. Grab each handle, sit on the bench, and get your arms into the starting position with your arms out to your sides and elbows bent. At this point your forearms should be lined up directly with the cable. Pull your shoulder blades down and back together. Plant your feet firmly on the ground.

Use your chest to bring your arms together with your arms straight in front of you. Think about squeezing your biceps in as if you were trying to bring them together to better engage your chest. Pause at the end position briefly, slowly control the weight back while bending your arms until your elbows reach the level of your torso, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid straightening your arms completely at the starting position and avoid bending your arms too much at the end position. This takes away tension from the chest and shifts more of the work to the biceps. Instead, keep your arms bent at the start and then straight at the end as if you were trying to touch your biceps together.

name: Seated Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Shoulder Press (*shoulder friendly)
steps: Set up an incline bench at about a 60 to 75 degree angle, typically 2 to 3 notches down from the highest position. Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on the bench with the dumbbells resting on your thighs. Kick the dumbbells up one at a time to get them up just over your shoulders. Plant your feet firmly on the ground. From here, bring your elbows forward in front of your shoulders with your palms facing each other.

Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. Press the weight up until your arms are straight and positioned directly over your shoulders and palms still facing each other. Lower the weight back down to the starting position, and then repeat.

name: Seated Weighted Calf Raises
steps: Sit on a flat bench with toes on 3–6 inch plates about hip width apart; knees near 90 degrees, dumbbells on thighs.
Press high onto toes with emphasis through big toe, then slowly lower heels and repeat.
cues: Do not use momentum/gravity; control the contraction and stretch on every rep.

name: Seated Weighted Calf Raises (Rest-Pause)
steps: Sit on a flat bench and elevate your toes onto a pair of weight plates in front of you set at about hip width apart. You ideally want about a 3-6 inch elevation. Grab a pair of dumbbells and hold them on your thighs. At this point your knees should be bent to 90 degrees with your toes on the edge of the platform and heels resting on the ground.

While keeping your toes on the platform, push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toe. Control your heel slowly back down to the bottom position and then repeat.
cues: Avoid mindlessly going through the reps and using momentum and gravity to bring you up and down. Instead, spend time controlling every single rep and feeling your calf contract then stretch.

name: Shoulder Press (Machine)
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles start around shoulder height and you can press without your shoulders shrugging up. Sit tall with your back against the pad, feet flat, and core tight.
Start with elbows slightly in front of your body. Press up until your arms are almost straight, then lower slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch at the bottom.
cues: Keep your head neutral, don’t arch your lower back to “cheat” reps, and don’t let your shoulders creep up toward your ears.

name: Side Leg Swings
steps: Keep your core tight and hold onto something beside you. Swing your leg left and right as far as your leg will go.
cues: This exercise is used to mobilize and warm up the hips and leg muscles for your leg movements.

name: Side Lying Hip Raise
steps: Start in a side-plank position on elbow with hips and knees on floor bent about 90 degrees.
Push through grounded knee and rise tall while lifting top leg toward ceiling; drive hips forward with glutes, then return hips back and legs together.
Complete one side before switching; use Side Lying Leg Raise if this is initially too difficult.
cues: Start with hips back and drive them forward; do not simply raise straight up and down.

name: Side Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lie on side with stacked hips, bottom leg bent, and head supported by hand.
Drive bottom knee into floor, brace, and raise straight top leg slightly back by driving heel diagonally up/back; pause, control down, and complete one side before switching.
cues: Slightly rotate toes toward floor as leg moves back to emphasize glute medius; Side Lying Hip Raise is the progression.

name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side with your legs bent and upper body supported through your elbow. Place your free hand on your opposite shoulder.
Brace your core and push your elbow and knees into the ground to raise your hips up towards the ceiling, and hold this position for the desired amount of time before switching sides.
cues: If this is too easy, you can progress it by extending your legs out to a full side plank position with your top foot planted slightly in front of your bottom leg and moving your free hand on top of your hips. Once that becomes easy, you can progress it further by introducing a rotation. While keeping your shoulders, torso, and upper leg in one straight line, try rotating your body towards the ground and then back up towards the ceiling. Again perform this for the desired amount of time on one side before switching sides and repeating.

name: Single Arm Overhead Rope Extensions
steps: With a rope attachment at its lowest position, pull the rope through, hold one end, face away from the cable, and step forward and slightly to the working-arm side; bring the arm over the head with the hand behind it.
Keeping the elbow locked in place, extend the hand fully in line with the arm; lower to the start and complete one side before switching.
cues: Keep the elbow fixed, avoid arching the lower back or flaring the ribs, and use full range of motion.

name: (Weighted) Single Leg Hip Thrusts
steps: Set mid-back on a knee/shin-height bench, align shins vertically over feet and body in a straight line.
Brace and squeeze glutes, lift one leg, lower hips about halfway to floor, then drive through planted heel to the top and pause with glute squeeze.
cues: Keep ribs down/core braced at top to prevent back arching and lower-back tension.

name: (Bodyweight) Single Leg Hip Thrusts
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent at 90 degrees in front of you; bring arms to sides with palms gripping floor, then raise one leg into the air at a 90-degree angle.

Drive the planted foot into the floor to bridge hips up while squeezing glutes of that leg; raise until torso is parallel with upper thigh and keep planted-leg knee at 90 degrees; avoid overarching lower back.
Lower hips to the starting position and repeat desired repetitions before switching legs; maintain hamstrings tension in the planted leg.
cues: Visible note: weight may be added with a backpack or object at the thigh/hip; a planted leg may be elevated to progress.

name: Single Leg Weighted Calf Raise
steps: Find a stable elevated platform or a weight plate you can use to perform your calf raises on. Place it next to a fixture to hold onto with support. Grab a dumbbell or weight plate in one hand and place your other hand on the fixture for support. Place the ball of your foot onto the edge of the platform with your foot facing straight forwards. The leg you use should be on the same side as where you’re holding the weight.

Brace your core and then slowly lower your heel down towards the floor. Pause briefly and then push straight up onto your toe as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toe. Control your heel slowly back down to the bottom position and then repeat. Finish your reps on one side and then turn over, switch the weight to your other arm, and switch legs to work your other calf.
cues: Avoid mindlessly going through the reps and using momentum and gravity to bring you up and down. Instead, spend time controlling every single rep and feeling your calf contract then stretch.

name: Single-Leg Leg Press
steps: Set low backrest/start position and safeties; place nonworking leg on ground and working foot middle-to-high on plate.
Release safeties, lower until knee is 90 degrees/vertical shin, press through heel to near-straight leg, rest one minute, then switch sides.
cues: Use a higher foot position so shin is vertical at bottom, not pushed forward toward toes.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell and stand on one leg. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee. Brace your core and keep your back flat.

Hinge at the hips by pushing them back while your free leg reaches behind you for balance. Lower until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstring of the standing leg, then drive your hips forward to return to standing.
cues: Keep your hips level and avoid twisting your torso.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
steps: Place a flat bench a couple feet behind bar, add thick bar pad/towel, and set feet so top position has 90-degree knees and vertical shins.
Tuck chin, brace, squeeze glutes, and drive hips up through heels while head/hips remain aligned; pause at top then lower hips to about halfway down under control.
cues: Keep ribs down and posteriorly tilt pelvis at top; lighten load if back is doing more work than glutes.

name: Smith Machine Squat
steps: Set the bar into its starting position at about the height of your mid-chest. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Duck under the bar and place it over the back of your shoulders, letting it rest on your upper traps. Lift it out of the rack by extending your legs, and then twist the bar to take it off the safety position. From here, set your feet. Your middle of your feet should be directly underneath the bar, but you can experiment with moving them forwards and see if it feels more comfortable. As for foot width, this will vary for everyone, but experiment with a stance that is just outside shoulder-width with your toes pointed outwards at about a 15 degree angle.

Plant your feet firmly into the ground, pull the bar down into your upper back, and engage your core. Take a deep breath in through your nose. From here, squat down by bending at your hips and knees. As you do so, the weight should be evenly distributed between your big toe, your little toe, and your heels. Your knees should also be bending slightly outwards in the same direction of your toes. Continue squatting down until your thighs reach at least parallel or slightly below. From here, while keeping your core engaged, exhale and reverse the movement by extending your legs, thinking about bringing the bar up towards the ceiling and exhaling as you do so.
cues: To properly set up your smith machine for this exercise, please refer to the exercise tutorial video for a step-by-step approach. If you find it difficult to reach full depth, you can try elevating your heels onto weight plates to help with ankle mobility.

name: Standing Banded Shoulder Press
steps: Stand shoulder width on a single loop band, lift ends to chin height and tuck elbows slightly forward.
Brace abs/squeeze glutes and press band straight overhead while moving head slightly back; return under control without lower-back arch.
cues: Progress to a single-arm banded press; avoid lower-back arching and press vertically instead of forward/back.

name: Standing Barbell Curl
steps: Grab a weighted bar or barbell with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart.

Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and away from your ears, and then while keeping your elbows locked in position, curl your hands up towards your shoulders. Once your arms reach roughly the level of your chest, control the weight back down until your arms fully straighten, and then repeat for another rep.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
steps: Set bar at armpit level, grip just outside shoulders with elbows below bar and vertical forearms, unrack, step back, and set shoulder-width stance.
Squeeze glutes and quads, brace, press straight overhead while moving chin slightly back then neutral after bar passes, and lock arms.
Lower with elbows roughly 45 degrees in front until bar reaches upper chest, pause/rebrace, and repeat.
cues: Keep this a strict upper-body press; do not use knee bend or leg drive.

name: Standing Cable Curls
steps: Use lowest pulley bar with shoulder-width underhand grip and small step back.
Brace/glute squeeze, curl toward shoulders with fixed elbows, then fully extend under control.
cues: Avoid swinging and lower under biceps control with elbows fixed.

name: Standing Cable Curls (Rest-Pause)
steps: Attach a bar to a pulley set at the lowest height. If you have access to a curled bar, use that, otherwise a straight bar can work. Grip the bar with an underhand shoulder-width grip and then take a small step back away from the cable, letting your arms hang down in front of your thighs.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to stabilize your body. Then, while keeping your elbow locked into place, curl the bar up towards your shoulders. Lower the weight back down to the starting position with your arms fully extended, and then repeat for another rep.
cues: Avoid swinging your body and elbows forward and back and excessively as you curl. Instead, lighten the weight, keep your elbow locked in place and control the weight. A little bit of forward elbow movement is fine, but it shouldn’t be excessive. Avoid letting the cable pull the weight down for you. Instead, use your biceps to slowly control the weight back down to the starting position before starting your next rep.

name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
steps: Set the pads on your shoulders and place the balls of your feet on the platform with heels hanging off. Keep knees straight or slightly soft, and hold the handles for balance.
Lower your heels slowly to feel a stretch in your calves, then press up onto your toes as high as you can. Pause briefly at the top, then lower again under control. Avoid bouncing or doing half reps.

name: Standing Dumbbell Curls
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and get in your standing position with your arms hanging by your sides with your palms turned in, facing the ceiling, and your feet planted firmly on the ground.

Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your core. While keeping both of your elbows locked into place, curl the weight up towards your shoulders. Lower the weight back down to the starting position, keeping your wrists in a flexed position throughout the curl. Once your arms fully straighten, repeat for another rep.

name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: Grab a pair of dumbbells and bring them up just over your shoulders. Set your feet by moving them shoulder width apart and bring your elbows forward slightly at about a 45-degree angle in front of your body.

Squeeze your glutes, flex your quads, and brace your core. Take a deep breath in through your nose and then exhale as you press the dumbbells straight up. Press until your arms are straight and positioned directly over your shoulders.

Inhale as you lower the dumbbells by dropping your elbows into a roughly 45-degree angle in front of your body until the dumbbells reach the level of your chin. Pause here briefly, restabilize your glutes and core if needed, and then continue for your next rep.
cues: Avoid bending your knees and using leg drive to move the weight up. This is a different exercise. Instead, keep this a strict press by only using your upper body to press the weight up.

name: Standing Face Pulls
steps: Move a cable to the top position. Using a double rope attachment, grab the rope in each hand with a neutral grip. Next, set the weight light and take a few steps back away from the pulley. From here, raise your arms so that they are straight and directly facing the pulley.

Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Pull your hands towards your face, trying to get the cable to the level of your forehead. As you do so, pull back with both your elbows and hands, such that at the end position your arms are positioned in a “biceps flexing” pose at a 90 degree angle with your hands directly over your elbows. From here, slowly raise your arms up into a Y position and then back down. Then, straighten your arms back to the starting position.
cues: If using a band, you would execute this the exact same way, and simply use a wide overhand grip on the band. The band will be quite challenging from even just a few steps away, so position yourself relatively closer to the band where there isn’t as much tension.

name: Standing High To Low Cable Flyes
steps: Stand between a cable setup with the pulleys set at the highest position. Grab each handle, take a step or two away from the cable, get into a staggered stance position for support, and bring your arms down and slightly in front of your body with your palms facing each other. You want to set up such that at this bottom position, the line of the cable is inline with your forearms and your arm in line with the side of your chest.

Set your weight, grab the handles and get back into your starting position. Brace your core. Control the weight up while slightly bending your elbows until you get to about shoulder height. Then, using your lower chest muscles, move your arms down and in together until they fully straighten. Think about pulling your arms together as if you were trying to touch your biceps together to move the weight to better engage your chest.

name: Standing Mid-Chest Cable Fly
steps: Set pulleys just above shoulders, take handles and staggered stance, slightly hinge forward, and position arms forward with palms facing and cable aligned with forearms.
Brace, return arms with bend until elbows align with torso, then use chest to bring arms together to straight while thinking of drawing biceps together.
cues: Keep arms bent at start and straight at end to retain chest tension.

name: Standing Mid-Chest Cable Fly (Rest-Pause)
steps: Stand between a cable setup with the pulleys to just above shoulder height. Grab each handle, take a couple steps away from the cable, get into a staggered stance position for support, bend over at your torso just slightly, and then bring your arms down straight in front of your body with your palms facing each other. You want to set up such that at this bottom position, the line of the cable is in line with your forearms.

Brace your core. Control the weight back while bending your arms until your elbows reach the level of your torso. Then, using your chest muscles, bring your arms in together until they fully straighten. Think about squeezing your biceps in as if you were trying to bring them together to better engage your chest.
cues: Avoid straightening your arms completely at the starting position and avoid bending your arms too much at the end position. This takes away tension from the chest and shifts more of the work to the biceps. Instead, keep your arms bent at the start and then straight at the end as if you were trying to touch your biceps together.
tips: Avoid straightening your arms completely at the starting position and avoid bending your arms too much at the end position. This takes away tension from the chest and shifts more of the work to the biceps. Instead, keep your arms bent at the start and then straight at the end as if you were trying to touch your biceps together.

name: Standing Underhand Dumbbell Fly
steps: Stand with a pair of light dumbbells in each hand and arms straight down by your sides. Pinch your shoulder blades together slightly and stick your chest out - you want to maintain this as you perform the movement.

By using an underhand grip such that your palm faces out in front of you, raise one dumbbell up and across your body by squeezing your chest of that side. Think about raising the dumbbell “up” and “in”. You should feel your chest contracting as you do so.

Return back to the starting position and then repeat with the other arm. Alternate until you perform the desired amount of repetitions on each arm, or more importantly until you reach muscular failure or close to it.

name: Standing Weighted Calf Raises (Barbell or Dumbbell)
steps: You can perform this movement either using a weighted barbell or with a pair of dumbbells in each hand. Grab a pair of dumbbells and place your feet about hip width apart facing forwards.

Brace your core and then push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toes. Then, control your heel slowly back down until they touch the ground, and repeat. Once you get good at this, you can progress it by adding a small 5 or 10 lb weight plate under each of your toes and perform it on there. Once you get good at that, you can use a larger weight plate or an elevated platform for a greater range of motion. It can be hard to balance so just be cautious when performing this so you don’t fall over. The same also applies if you were using barbells.
cues: Feet hip width apart, elevate toes on weight plate, press up on big toes.

name: Standing Weighted Calf Raises (Barbell or Dumbbell) (Rest-Pause)
steps: You can perform this movement either using a weighted barbell or with a pair of dumbbells in each hand. Grab a pair of dumbbells and place your feet about hip width apart facing forwards.

Brace your core and then push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toes. Then, control your heel slowly back down until they touch the ground, and repeat. Once you get good at this, you can progress it by adding a small 5 or 10 lb weight plate under each of your toes and perform it on there. Once you get good at that, you can use a larger weight plate or an elevated platform for a greater range of motion. It can be hard to balance so just be cautious when performing this so you don’t fall over. The same also applies if you were using barbells.
cues: Feet hip width apart, elevate toes on weight plate, press up on big toes.
tips: Feet hip width apart, elevate toes on weight plate, press up on big toes.

name: Sumo Deadlift (*lower back friendly)
steps: Start with a barbell on the ground. If you have access to big bumper plates, load the bar with those. If you aren’t going to be using any weight or only have access to smaller weight plates, either elevate the bar onto a rack, weight stack, or any elevated platform so that the bar starts at about the level of your shins. Stand with the bar over your midfoot. Take a sumo stance by moving your feet out wide, to at least outside of shoulder-width with your toes pointed out. You can tell if your feet are too wide based on your mobility if when you go down to grab the bar, your knees cave inward and you can’t keep your knees out towards your toes. Play around with this to see what feels best.

Next, get down to grip the bar by pushing your hips back and then bending your knees out and forward towards the direction of your toes. Grab the bar with a double overhand grip with your arms hanging straight down right at shoulder-width apart, which should be inside your knees. From here, bring the bar as close to your shins as possible and tuck your chin down to align your neck with your spine by gazing at the floor just a few feet in front of you.

Stabilize your body by thinking about bending the bar in half towards you by engaging your lat muscles, and then pull your chest up and hips down to wedge yourself into the bar. From here, brace your core and pull the slack out of the bar by lightly pulling up against it and pushing your feet away from the floor. From here, while maintaining a straight back and keeping your chest up, pull up on the bar while pushing your feet down against the floor. As you do so, the bar should travel in a perfectly straight line up over your midfoot and should be kept as close to your body as possible. Your knees should also be pointing out, staying in line with the direction of your toes. Once the weight passes your knees, drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to finish the lift. From here, control the weight back down by first pushing your hips back and then once the weight passes your knees, bending your knees until the weights touch the ground. Again, keep the bar as close to your thighs and knees as possible. You can choose to either perform touch and go reps, just lightly tapping the ground with the weights each rep, or you can choose to let the weights fully settle on the ground and reset your form before going into the next rep.
cues: For the sumo deadlift, since the exercise is quite technical, it is recommended that you watch the exercise tutorial video. If you still have trouble with rounding your back as you pull, try lightening the weight and also consider elevating the starting position onto weight plates to shorten the range of motion. This is especially helpful for taller individuals or those with certain hip structures that make getting into the deadlift position difficult. You don’t need to lift from the floor unless you’re planning to compete as a powerlifter.

name: Supine Press Machine
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up around mid chest. Keep your feet flat and your upper back pressed into the pad. Start with the handles near your chest and wrists straight.

Press the handles away until your arms are almost straight, then lower slowly until you feel a good stretch in your chest without shoulder discomfort. Keep your shoulders down and back and don’t let them roll forward as you press.

name: Swiss Ball Leg Curls
steps: Lay on your back with your legs straight and heels together placed on top of a swiss ball.

Brace your core, and then use your glutes to push your hips forward into the air until your torso makes a straight line with your legs. Maintain this position as you curl your feet towards your butt as far as you can without breaking form. Reverse by extending your legs back until they are almost fully straight, and repeat for another rep.
cues: When doing these, think “heels in and hips up” throughout each rep. If this is too difficult, you can try shortening the range of motion by not bringing your legs in as far, or you can simply hold your two legs out straight for 30-60 seconds to build up the strength to do the movement.

name: T-Bar Row
steps: Load the T-bar and step into position so the handle is centered under your chest. Set your feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart, bend your knees, and hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly 30–45° above parallel. Keep your back flat and brace your core like someone’s about to punch you in the stomach.

Grab the handle and start with your arms fully extended so your shoulder blades can open up at the bottom. Pull by driving your elbows back (think elbow to hip), squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly back to a full stretch. Don’t bounce off the bottom.
Avoid turning it into a whole-body heave: no torso rocking, no shrugging your shoulders up, and no rounding your lower back.
cues: If grip is the limiter, use straps so your back, not your hands, does the work.

name: Tibialis Raise
steps: Stand with back against wall and heels on floor, or use a tibialis machine.
Lift toes/front of feet toward shins, pause, then lower slowly without rocking.

name: Toes-Elevated Smith Machine Calf Raises
steps: Set the bar into its starting position at about the height of your shoulders. Then, place an elevated platform or weight plate underneath the bar such that the end of it where your toes will go is positioned directly under the bar or a few inches in front of it. Load the bar with appropriate weight, and then grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Place the bar over the back of your shoulders onto your upper traps. Place the balls of your feet onto the edge of the platform or weight plate at about hip width apart with your feet facing forwards. Lift the bar out of the rack.

Brace your core and then slowly lower your heel down towards the floor. Pause briefly and then push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toes. Control your heel slowly back down to the bottom position and then repeat. Continue until you finish the desired number of reps and then re-rack the bar.
cues: Avoid mindlessly going through the reps and using momentum and gravity to bring you up and down. Instead, spend time controlling every single rep and feeling your calf contract then stretch.

name: Toes-Elevated Smith Machine Calf Raises (Rest-Pause)
steps: Set the bar into its starting position at about the height of your shoulders. Then, place an elevated platform or weight plate underneath the bar such that the end of it where your toes will go is positioned directly under the bar or a few inches in front of it. Load the bar with appropriate weight, and then grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Place the bar over the back of your shoulders onto your upper traps. Place the balls of your feet onto the edge of the platform or weight plate at about hip width apart with your feet facing forwards. Lift the bar out of the rack.

Brace your core and then slowly lower your heel down towards the floor. Pause briefly and then push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toes. Control your heel slowly back down to the bottom position and then repeat. Continue until you finish the desired number of reps and then re-rack the bar.
cues: Avoid mindlessly going through the reps and using momentum and gravity to bring you up and down. Instead, spend time controlling every single rep and feeling your calf contract then stretch.

name: Towel Curl Isometric
steps: Step on one end of towel/band and pull with hand to create biceps tension.
Hold 30 seconds and keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce pull intensity if pain exceeds 4/10.

name: Towel Lateral Raise Isometric
steps: Step on one end of towel/band, pull arms straight to sides, and hold 30 seconds.
Keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Pull less hard if pain is above 4/10.

name: Towel Overhead Extensions Isometric
steps: Hold towel/band vertically behind back; keep bottom hand still and pull upward with top hand.
Hold 30 seconds and keep pain at or below 3–4/10.
cues: Reduce pulling force if pain is above 4/10.

name: Towel Overhead Press Isometric
steps: Secure towel/band beneath knee.
With arm bent 90 degrees, pull upward as hard as able and hold 30 seconds.
cues: Keep pain intensity at or below 3–4/10.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift (*lower back friendly)
steps: Start with the trap bar on the ground and weights on each side. Step into the middle of the bar and position yourself so that the handles are in line with the middle of your feet. Set your feet at about hip-width apart and toes pointed outwards slightly. Get down to grip the bar by pushing your hips back and then bending your knees. Grab each handle with your arms completely straight. From here, tuck your chin down to align your neck with your spine by gazing at the floor just a few feet in front of you.

Pull your chest up and hips down to wedge yourself into the bar. From here, brace your core and pull the slack out of the bar by lightly pulling up against it and pushing your feet away from the floor. Next, while maintaining a straight back and keeping your chest up, pull up on the bar while pushing your feet down against the floor and then driving your hips forward until you stand up fully. From here, control the weight back down by first pushing your hips back and then bending your knees until the weights touch the ground. You can choose to either perform touch and go reps, just lightly tapping the ground with the weights each rep, or you can choose to let the weights fully settle on the ground and reset your form before going into the next rep.
cues: Avoid pulling the bar right off the ground without getting rid of the slack. Instead, before your rep, pull up slightly on the bar to get rid of the slack and to create tension in your arms and lower body without the bar lifting up. Then, from here, you can initiate your rep by exerting your full effort.

name: Tricep Bar Pushdowns
steps: Set high pulley with straight/EZ bar, step back and slightly hinge so arms clear body, with elbows at sides.
Brace, extend forearms fully by contracting triceps, then return slowly with elbows fixed.
cues: Keep elbows locked and do not swing.

name: Tricep Dips
steps: Use a dip machine with parallel handles. Grip the handles and get to the starting position with your arms locked and legs bent. Engage your core and keep your torso upright.
Slowly lower your body by tucking your elbows. Go as low as is comfortable for you, but aim to get your upper arm parallel with the floor.
Push through your palms and extend your elbows to get back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Triceps Kickback
steps: Hold dumbbell, hinge forward with flat back/core tight, raise upper arm close to side and parallel to floor.
Extend dumbbell back to full elbow extension, pause, then return slowly without swinging or dropping upper arm.

name: Walking Lunges (Quad Focused)
steps: Hold dumbbells at sides, stand tall with feet together, and brace.
Step forward, descend down and slightly forward by driving the front knee toward toes, then push through the front leg to return to feet together before alternating.
cues: Use the rear leg as a kickstand: 80–90% of load should stay in the front leg.

name: Wall Push Isometric
steps: Lean forward against a wall.
Push into the wall using both arms.
Maintain this held position for a duration of 30 seconds.
Monitor your pain levels; the intensity should not exceed a three or four out of 10.
cues: Reduce the force of your push if the pain level rises above a four

name: Wall Slides
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet together positioned a few steps away from it. Raise your arms up into a 90 degree angle against the wall. Engage your core to flatten your lower back against the wall. At this point you want your head, hands, elbows, lower back, and butt to all be touching the wall. If this is too difficult you can step your feet forward a couple steps more.

Slide your arms up against the wall as if you were performing a shoulder press, and continue as far up as you can while keeping your elbows and hands in contact with the wall. Lower back down to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Avoid excessively arching your lower back off the wall and avoid losing contact with your arms against the wall. To ease the difficulty, take steps further away from the wall and avoid going too far up with your arms until you build the needed strength and mobility overtime.

name: Weakpoint Pause Bench Press
steps: This exercise will be used to strengthen the weakest point in the bench press.
You will perform a regular bench press, but using about 10-20% less weight and adding a 1 second pause based on where you are weakest in the bench.
Weakpoint 1:
If you usually fail or struggle the most at the very bottom right off your chest, then your 1 second pause will be at the very bottom on your chest.
Weakpoint 2:
If you usually fail in the middle, pause at the middle about 2-4 inches off your chest.
Weakpoint 3:
If you usually fail at the top, then pause near the top when your elbows make roughly a 90 degree angle.

name: Weighted Crunches
steps: Lay your lower back on the mat and plant your feet in front of you with your knees bent at 90 degrees.

Place your hands across your chest, contract your abs hard, and then curl your spine forwards bringing your chest up towards your knees. Continue up as far as you can, past the point where your torso makes a 45 degree angle with the ground. Use your abs to control your body back down to the starting position, letting your back extend over the ab mat, and then continue for another rep.
cues: An alternative to the ab mat is to use a rolled up towel and place that under your low back or to use a stability ball to perform your crunches on. Once you can do 3 sets of 15 controlled reps with your hands on your chest, you can make the movement more difficult by placing your hands behind your head. Once that becomes easy, you can start overloading with weight by holding a weight plate or dumbbell at your chest.

name: Weighted External Rotations
steps: Use a light weight, keep the elbow locked, and rotate hand up towards ceiling then back down. Repeat on the other side.
cues: This exercise is used to warm up the rotator cuff muscles.
tips: This exercise is used to warm up the rotator cuff muscles.

name: Weighted Step Ups (*knee friendly)
steps: Hold dumbbells by sides in front of a stable knee- to mid-thigh-height bench or box.
Brace, step one foot onto the platform and stand to straight leg while the other leg stays just above it; lower under control, bring feet together, and alternate sides.
cues: Treat the planted trailing leg only as a balance kickstand: use 80–90% of weight on the working leg.

name: Wide Grip Barbell Upright Row
steps: Use a wide overhand grip about 1.5× shoulder width, brace core, and squeeze glutes.
Raise with elbows bent about 90 degrees and forearms forward; adjust grip until forearms are level, raise to shoulder height, then lower to straight arms.
cues: Keep forearms horizontal at top; do not let them drop/internally rotate the shoulders.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
steps: Get into a plank position with your hands under your shoulders and feet together. From here, lunge forward by bringing your right foot up as high as you can, ideally next to where your right hand is. You should feel a deep stretch in your groin muscles of your front leg and the hip flexors of your back leg as you do this.
Take your right hand, place it on your knee and push your knee out and back and then forward and back a few times to loosen up the hips and ankles.

To deepen the stretch even more, drop your right elbow as far towards the ground as you can while rotating your upper body down towards the ground. As you do this, try to keep your right knee pushed out rather than letting it collapse inwards.

To now open up the mid and upper back, rotate your entire upper body up and to the right and reach your right arm as far overhead as you can. If you can, try to keep your back leg as straight as possible as you do so. Then, reach back down and repeat this for 5 quality reps or about 30 seconds in total before switching to the next side.
cues: To make it easier, you can keep your leg bent or your knee on the ground and work towards straightening it more and more overtime.

name: Wrist Curls (Cable)
steps: Grip the handle with your palm facing up and keep your elbow locked at your side to stabilize the forearm.
Curl the handle downward by flexing only the wrist, squeezing the wrist flexors at the bottom of the movement.
Return slowly under control, allowing the wrist to fully extend before starting the next repetition.

name: Wrist Curls (Dumbbell)
steps: Set the bench 2–3 notches from the bottom so it sits at a 45–60° angle. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and position your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge, palm facing up. Keep your forearm completely still.

Allow the dumbbell to roll slightly toward your fingers, then curl it up by bending only at the wrist. Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly under control. Use a load you can manage without turning the movement into an arm curl.

name: Wrist Extension (Dumbbell)
steps: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench with the backs of your hands facing up and wrists hanging off the edge. Keep your forearms still.
Lower the dumbbell by letting the wrist bend down, then raise it by lifting the back of your hand up. Move slowly and keep the range controlled.

name: Wrist Extensions (Cables)
steps: Set a low cable and grip a handle with the back of your hand facing up. Support your forearm so only your wrist moves.
Extend the wrist by lifting the back of your hand up, pause, then lower slowly. Keep your elbow locked in place and avoid turning it into a full arm movement.

name: Zercher Squat
steps: Set a bar in a rack around waist to mid stomach height. Step in close and hold the bar in the crook of your elbows, keeping your hands together and elbows pointed slightly forward. Keep your chest up and core tight.

Step back and squat down by sitting your hips between your heels. Keep the bar close to your body and your torso tall. Drive back up through your whole foot to stand. Avoid rounding your upper back or letting your elbows drop.
